articleTitle: The Effects of Rotor Delta and Embrace Parameters on the Performance of Flux-Switching Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: One of the types of generators used in variable-speed wind turbine applications in microgrids is the flux-switching generator. Due to the double-salient structure of flux-switching generators, torque ripples and harmonic content are high. In addition, the magnetic flux density in the stator and rotor teeth is elevated. To overcome these issues, improvements can be made in the machine's design parameters. In this study, the effects of rotor pole skew (delta) and coil-pole pitch ratio (embrace) parameters on the machine�s output values for a 1200 min-1, 200 Hz, and 260W design were examined. It was observed that changes in the pole skew and coil-pole pitch ratio parameters affect torque, flux linkage, and induced voltage values, and can reduce magnetic stresses

articleTitle: Evaluation of Background Subtraction and Pattern Recognition Methods for Classification of GPR B-Scan Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the performance comparison of background subtraction, feature extraction and machine learning based classification methods on GPR (Ground Penetrating Radar) data obtained from buried objects was made. Filtering, pre-processing and post-processing techniques were used, and after making the buried objects more distinct, the data was classified using machine learning methods. The developed methods were tested on a real data set consisting of 1040 data and 6 different classes and the performance comparison of the methods was made.

articleTitle: Performance of Alamouti STBC NOMA Signals in Rayleigh Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a 3-user NOMA structure consisting of a single receiver and a single transmitter was used, using the Nonorthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technique developed for 5G, the new generation communication technology, and a 2x1 (2 Transmitting Antenna - 1 Receiving Antenna) structure with 3 users at different distances. ) The performances of the Alamouti Space-Time Block Coding (STBC) NOMA structure and the 2x2 (2 Transmitting Antennas-2 Receiving Antennas) Alamouti Space-Time Block Coding (STBC) NOMA structure with three users at different distances are compared in the Rayleigh Channel. Simulations were carried out in the MATLAB program depending on the Power variable (P). Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation method was used in the simulations. Performance analyzes were examined by comparing the graphs of changes in Bit Error Rate (BER) in the simulations performed. As a result of examining the graphics, it was concluded that 2x2 Alamouti STBC NOMA has better BER performance for each user (Near User, Middle User, Remote User) in Rayleigh Channel compared to 2x1 Alamouti STBC NOMA and the NOMA structure consisting of a single receiver and transmitter.

articleTitle: Low Noise Amplifier and Reflective Switch Design in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology for X and Ku Band Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the design of low noise amplifer (LNA) and reflective switch, developed using 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS techonology is presented for X-band (8-12 GHz) and Ku-band (12-18 GHz) radar applications. The LNA and reflective switch are critical components due to their effect on the sensitivity performance of radar receiver systems. Therefore, the proposed designs were optimized and improved considering sensitivity performance of the system. The designed LNA provides flat 20 dB gain with a maximum variety of 0.2 dB and its noise figure is below 1.8 dB across the desired frequency band. It operates with 2.5V supply voltage and consumes 40 mW of power. P1-dB and IIP3 values are -16 dBm and -6 dBm respectively. The reflective switch has a maximum insertion loss of 1.5 dB along the desired band and provides isolation of -50 dB at the center frequency of 13 GHz and below -30 dB at the edge of frequency band.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Geometrical Losses on the Quality Factor in FSO Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, an examination dependent on the variation of the quality factor (Q) associated with geometric losses, which constitute a significant portion of the losses arising from the external environment in free-space optical (FSO) communication systems, has been carried out. Geometric losses were examined under different atmospheric conditions, channel configurations and distances. Two main systems, namely optical fiber and FSO transmission lines, were used in the study. Losses under different transmission conditions in the transmission line were equalized by varying the length of the optical fiber based on the FSO communication system. Thus, the aim was to reveal the geometric losses occuring in the FSO communication system. The variation of these losses was observed using two channel and four channel wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) techniques. As a result of the study, it was observed that when using the same transmission line, two-channel systems achieved a higher quality factor compared to four-channel systems. The variation in the quality factor with respect to the transmission line has shown dependency on distance.

articleTitle: Systematic Design of High-Pass Graph Filters via Low-Pass Graph Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In traditional signal processing, signals are filtered to obtain information components within time signals by eliminating the noise components. In many applications, towards a similar goal, graph signals used in modeling complex systems need to be filtered appropriately. For this purpose, the field of graph signal processing has emerged by combining traditional signal processing methods and graph theory. Various graph filter definitions and designs have been proposed in the literature, mainly low-pass graph filters. In this study, we propose a systematic method for designing high-pass graph filters using a graph modulation operator together with existing low-pass filters and present simulation examples that include the use of the designed filters in filtering graph signals.

articleTitle: STSeqGNN - Konum-Zaman Tabanlı Hareket Karakterizasyonu
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Spatio-temporal finger-printing is an active research topic, which is of critical importance in mobility analysis. Various neural network models working on LBSN data have been presented within the framework of TUL (Trajectory-user linking). However, to the best of our knowledge, there are no studies on neural networks for sequential spatio-temporal data like GPS in the literature. Therefore, here we present the STSeqGNN model, which can process sequential spatiotemporal data. Our model can process the graph structure of the map and the time dimension of the data. Our model also can use movement information and basic statistical values for better finger-printing performance. We present our test results with the evaluation metric accuracy at k. Our model achieves more than 99% accuracy across different datasets.

articleTitle: Extending the ZVS Range of Quasi Resonant Inverter Topology used Induction Hobs
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a high-frequency induction cooktop system utilizing a quasi-resonant inverter topology that can provide soft switching in the main voltage range of 150V-250 VAC and input power range of 1000-2000 W is presented. The factors affecting the soft switching range in the proposed induction cooktop design are explained, and design parameters for achieving a wide soft switching range are determined. These parameters were optimized to design an induction cooktop system with a maximum power output of 2000 W. The proposed design was simulated in a computer environment, and it was observed that soft switching was achieved within the 1000-2000 W power range. The design, validated through simulation, was implemented, and the waveforms confirmed that soft switching was maintained within the 1000-2000 W power range.

articleTitle: Investigation of Force Measurement Processes of Load Cells Using STM32G030F6P6TR Microcontroller and HX711 24 Bit Analog to Digital
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Load cells are sensors that convert forces into electronic signals and are commonly used in weight and force measurements. This study explores converting the force on a load cell into an electronic signal. The circuit board design employs the STM32G030F6P6TR microcontroller and HX711 24-bit analog-to-digital converter to process the load cell signal. Serial connection topology ensures data communication between the circuit board and a computer. For user interaction, measured data is displayed on an OLED screen and monitored via a computer terminal. Calibration parameters were set using calibrated weights. Once the accuracy of the weight data was verified, it was converted into force. A tare function was applied to eliminate excess weight on the load cell, ensuring accurate calibration. The results, including weight, calculated force, and maximum force, were displayed and reported on the OLED and terminal screens.

articleTitle: Energy Management Potential Analysis for Peak Demand Reduction for Energy Communities Containing Urban Houses and Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Peak demand causes imbalance between demand and production and additional costs in grids and energy communities (EC). Due to their structure, hospitals are constantly in use by a large number of people and their energy needs are different from household buildings. EC are subsystems consisting of specific electrical loads, electricity generation and storage systems. This study uses solar panels as a source with the grid, which appeal to both domestic and commercial users. In EC, which consists of a total of 375 households, a hospital with a capacity of 709 beds, 107 electric vehicle charging stations and a battery group with an installed power of 300 kW and a capacity of 591 kWh in the hospital, peak demand reduction is provided through energy management and scenarios are created according to hourly changing dynamic grid prices, resulting costs are compared. There are 303 residential; 215 commercial type solar panels installed in the EC. EC operates constantly connected to the grid under investigation.

articleTitle: Detection of Lower Extremity Anisomelia with the Developed Force Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the effectiveness of the developed force platform in detecting lower extremity anisomelia Is comprehensively examined. The experimental results show that the participant diagnosed with anisomelia lifted their longer leg off the ground slightly after their other leg during jumping. The data obtained revealed a time difference of 45.44 ms in jumping performance of individuals with anisomelia, while this duration was only 11.36 ms in normal participants. It is emphasized in the literature that the differences in the mobility of individuals with anisomelia may increase the challenges they could face in daily life and potentially lead to various musculoskeletal issues. These findings indicate that the force platform holds significant potential for assessing and monitoring the rehabilitation processes and performance of individuals with anisomelia. Future studies aim to enhance the reliability and effectiveness of the system through comprehensive research on different age groups and types of anisomelia. Moreover, the advantages of such methods being less invasive and more reliable present important benefits for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Improving Predictive Maintenance Performance with Limited Data under Different Operating Conditions with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper aims to provide an effective solution to the problem of data constraints that are frequently encountered in artificial intelligence applications. A combination of deep learning techniques is proposed to overcome the challenges related to data access and quality in the remaining useful life (RUL) estimation of industrial equipment. Using data obtained from equipment operating in different operating conditions, the research aims to perform RUL prediction of equipment operating in another operational context with the highest accuracy at the lowest cost. The applied methodology includes various Transfer Learning algorithms and domain adaptation techniques. Experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves a significant improvement in RUL prediction performance by 60% on average compared to the scenario where the proposed methods are not applied. The work contributes to the fields of predictive maintenance and asset management in industrial systems, offering the potential to optimize reliability and cost where data constraints are common like defence industry.

articleTitle: Resonance in Transformers and Energizing
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Transformers are the most efficient, fixed electrical machines for converting electricity into usable form in the energy system. In transmission and distribution lines, they increase the voltage, decrease the current and increase the current, decrease the voltage. The power value remains constant and energy is transmitted with maximum efficiency. Core structure and winding design have a significant effect on the amplitude of the transformer inrush currents. Commissioning of transformers is important for lifespan and operation. In some cases, inrush currents can be as strong as short circuit currents. It will cause abnormal noise in the transformer for a while. In this study, the scenario that may occur during the commissioning of transformers is discussed. Electromagnetic analysis was performed for the inrush current in the sample transformer, the incident was investigated and the fault development was detailed.

articleTitle: Using Deep Learning Algorithms for Cyberattack Detection in IEC 61850-Based Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a deep learning-based Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is developed for power systems using the IEC 61850 protocol. Existing literature primarily focuses on detecting cyberattacks under steady-state conditions, often ignoring scenarios involving operational faults. This limitation reduces the effectiveness of these approaches in real-world operations. To address this, the study proposes a method that distinguishes between natural faults and cyber-attack-induced faults. A 735 kV power system was modeled in MATLAB/Simulink and communicated real-time with Linux-based Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs). It was shown that False Data Injection (FDI) attacks could manipulate protection systems, potentially leading to incorrect power outages. Among deep learning models trained and tested on data from 1,200 simulations, Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) outperformed LSTM and GRU models. This study is a significant step toward to developing deep learning-based IDS for practical use in power systems.

articleTitle: Development of Greedy Auction-based Distributed Decision-Making Algorithm and Agent Communication Language in Swarm Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Distributed decision-making algorithms, which are task sharing methods that implement communication between unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), provide speed and practicality. In this study, Greedy Auction Based Distributed Decision-Making Algorithm (GCAA) and agent communication language development are presented in swarm UAVs. In order to provide communication between agents, air-to-air (A2A), air-to-ground (A2G) communication channels are created and the negotiation phase is provided through these communication channels. The proposed decentralized algorithm is compared with the centralized algorithm in environments where communication is interrupted and uninterrupted, and simulation results are given in MATLAB. It is observed that the developed distributed decision-making algorithm has shorter system cost, number of disabled agents and task duration depending on system parameters compared to the centralized algorithm.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data Using Unsupervised Machine Learning and Statistical Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Anomaly detection in signal data is crucial for identifying unexpected patterns and deviations without labeled data, making it suitable for real-world scenarios with infrequent and diverse anomalies. The implementation of machine learning-based detection methods is becoming popular due to their efficiency and time-saving nature. Effective anomaly detection is in constant need in the automotive industry, where it can be applied in functional integrity checks, calibration optimization, failure detection, regulatory compliance standards, and more. Due to NOx emissions from combustion engines having detrimental effects on the environment, this paper evaluates the effectiveness of unsupervised learning methods, including one-class SVM and isolation forest, alongside statistical techniques such as modified z-score and empirical analysis, in detecting anomalies within the engine out NOx mass flow signal. By providing a detailed comparison and analysis, this paper offers insights into their practical applications in time series data.

articleTitle: Optimization of Shielding Effectiveness for Ventilation Panels in Military Applications Using Root Solution Methods and Various Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the advancement of technology, electromagnetic environmental conditions have become influential in the operational performance of devices. Consequently, in the context of communication and information security, military standards have evolved to implement more stringent measures for electromagnetic conditions. Specifically, for shielded enclosures in military communication facilities, ensuring compliance with performance criteria such as MIL-PRF-32675 and NATO 6516/SHCPE/86-88 has become a significant engineering challenge. This study addresses the optimization of shielding effectiveness for ventilation panels, which are required in enclosed spaces and contribute to a reduction in shielding performance. The optimization was conducted using root solutions and various algorithms based on panel geometry, aiming to achieve maximum air flow while meeting the desired minimum shielding effectiveness values. The optimization results were simulated using the CST Studio Suite program, validating both the optimization process and panel design. The findings and additional considerations for further development are presented in the results section.

articleTitle: Role of Solar Power Plants in Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions and Their Integration to Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In modern cities, high energy consumption leads to significant greenhouse gas emissions, most of which originate from grid-based sources, highlighting the need for reform in energy production. The integration of renewable energy plants into urban grids is crucial for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and selecting the appropriate energy source and installation site is critical in this process. This study focuses on integrating Solar Power Plants (SPPs) into existing structures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and ensure the sustainability of vacant lands. Accordingly, an example SPP project model was developed to explore how using building rooftops as plant areas can reduce greenhouse gas emissions from grid-based electricity consumption.

articleTitle: Measurement of Geometric Dimensions of Hexagonal Type Washer Parts Using Machine Vision-Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a method is proposed for measuring the geometric properties of hexagonal precision adjustment washers. The method primarily involves measuring the hypothetical diameter that encompasses the outermost part of the hexagon and the key slot dimensions of the hexagon. For the key slot dimension, subpixel-based edge detection is performed following a preprocessing step. Subsequently, the enclosing circle and diameter are estimated based on the detected points. For the key slot measurement, the first step involves Hough transform-based line detection. By predicting the equations of the detected lines, the distances between the opposing lines are computed. According to the results, both the proposed diameter measurement algorithm and the key slot measurement algorithm function with an average error of approximately 13 μm in the utilized dataset. When considering part tolerances and average error amounts, it is concluded that the proposed algorithms are successful and feasible for practical use.

articleTitle: Graphene Based Fractal Structure 5G Microstrip Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: A graphene based 5G microstrip patch antenna with a fractal structure is proposed. Recently, it has been seen that 5G microstrip patch antenna studies are open to development. In line with the research, it was decided to use graphene in antenna coating thanks to its high electromagnetic, mechanical, electrical and thermal properties. This coating will be done using the EPD (Electrophoretic Deposition) method. EPD method and coating stages will be given in the paper. By using fractal structures in the antenna design, the design is intended to be unique. Necessary parameters will be calculated theoretically and drawings and simulations will be carried out in computer environment. In future studies, the antenna design will be physically printed and coated with graphene. After the coating, the necessary electromagnetic and electrical tests will be performed and compared with the theoretical study.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of a New Buck-Boost Power Converter for Advanced Target Tracking Radar Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In satellite applications, the active operational time of the satellite is largely dependent on the lifespan of the battery. The charge and discharge currents of the battery have a significant impact on its lifespan. Therefore, power converters used in power supplies must be designed with this in mind to prevent the battery from being exposed to large currents. The power converter proposed in this study has been developed to enable energy transfer from the battery to the supercapacitor while the ATTR (Advanced Target Tracking Radar) load is active. With this approach, it is possible to reduce the amplitudes of charge and discharge currents, thereby extending the battery life and increasing the satellite's mission duration. Additionally, this converter can vary the input voltage without encountering stability issues. The mathematical model of this new converter, which combines the Weinberg and buck converters, has been provided, simulated, and its results have been presented.

articleTitle: Creation of Positive and Zero Sequence Equivalent Circuit Models for Three-Winding Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: To calculate short circuit currents correctly and to make protection and coordination settings, it is important to measure the positive and zero sequence impedances of power transformers, which are indispensable elements of the power system. In this study, the measurements and mathematical operations performed to obtain the positive and zero sequence impedance models of three-phase transformers obtained from three-winding single-phase transformers are explained in detail. For the verification studies of the positive and zero sequence impedance equivalent circuit model of the single-phase 1 kVA, 276/120/54 V, mantel type, YNyn+d connection group test transformer, phase-ground fault was experimentally carried out in Kocaeli University Facility Research and Application Unit Laboratory. Model verification studies were supported by performing phase-ground fault in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. Phase-ground fault solution was performed with symmetrical components by replacing the transformer equivalent circuit obtained from positive and zero sequence measurement results. The obtained equivalent circuit model was verified with simulation study and experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Solar Radiation Forecasting using Multi-Reservoir Computing and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Accurate and reliable predictions are crucial for optimizing the efficiency of solar energy systems. Reservoir computing, particularly in the forecasting of complex time series, is distinguished by its low computational costs and high accuracy. Multi-reservoir architectures offer a more flexible and robust framework for data modeling. In this study, the multi-reservoir computing (M-RC) method is employed for solar radiation forecasting, and its performance is analyzed using normalized solar radiation data for Sivas, obtained from the National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB. The method achieved the lowest error rate with a mean square error (MSE) of 0.0471. The results indicate that M-RC is an effective approach, particularly in complex and dynamic systems, enabling more accurate compared to classical methods.

articleTitle: Comparative Electrical Load Prediction with Machine Learning and Fractional Calculus Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Forecasting short-term electrical loads is crucial for power supply system management, sustainability and upkeep. There are two main objectives for this study. First, it seeks to provide a thorough comparison of deep learning and machine learning techniques while forecasting for 1-h-ahead and 1-d-ahead. To remove any disruptions from the time series and comprehend its dynamics, the study also concentrates on mathematically modelling electricity load data using fractional calculus.

articleTitle: Tek Yönlü Hat İçi Optik Yükseltme ile 70 km Tek Modlu Fiber Üzerinde Üçüncü Şahıs İhlal Algılamaya Yönelik Uzun Mesafeli Dağıtık Akustik Algılama (DAS)
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study examines the implementation of FOTAS, a longdistance Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) system, through single-sided inline optical amplification over a 70 km fiber span. This configuration extends the sensing range to 140 km in a dualchannel setup, enabling reliable detection across extended distances. The phase-sensitive OTDR system successfully detected excavation events at a 72 km distance on a single channel. By employing Raman amplification and wavelength filtering techniques, the system achieved enhanced signal detection and high sensitivity over long distances. The findings underscore the effectiveness of phase-sensitive DAS technology in real-world applications, highlighting its potential for scalable and high-performance sensing in various industries.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Antenna-Fed Switchable Beam-Scanning High-Gain Wide Band Parabolic Reflector Design
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a planar Vivaldi antenna-fed reflector antenna is presented for wide-band (L and S band) applications. The proposed antenna operates between 500 MHz and 4.6 GHz. The Vivaldi feed antenna is designed on a low-costFR4 substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm. In this design, innovative approaches to gain enhancement techniques such as corrugations and directive elements are used. The standing wave ratio of the antenna is less than 2 throughout the operating band and the gain is 26 dBi. The analyses are designed using a full-wave three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation tool.

articleTitle: Torque Improvement in a Seven-Phase Machine by Injecting the Higher Current Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the torque increase due to current harmonics injectection into a seven-phase machine was investigated analytically and using finite element analysis software (FEA). It is possible to increase torque by injecting current harmonics in a multi-phase machine. Torque in a seven-phase machine can be increased by injecting the third and fifth current harmonics. In this study, firstly, the torque increase with current harmonics in a seven-phase machine was investigated analytically. Then, in order to prove these theoretical findings, a permanent magnet seven-phase machine design was made in an FEA software. Three different simulation experiments were conducted using this design. In the first simulation, the machine was driven only with the fundamental component of the current. In the second simulation, the third harmonic was injected additional to the fundamental component of the current. In the last simulation experiment, the fifth harmonic was injected in addition to the fundamental component and the third harmonic. As a result of these three simulations, it was observed that the torque of the machine increased significantly without ripple for each injected harmonic.

articleTitle: The Role of Speed-Related Frequencies in Vibration-Based Mechanical Faults Detection in Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In induction motors, possible faults can affect the dynamic performance of the motor and reduce the overall efficiency of the motor-driven systems. Therefore, it is crucial to detect potential faults early and accurately. This study investigates the role of speed-related frequencies in vibration-based detection of mechanical faults in induction motors. For this purpose, a test setup is built, and different mechanical faults are created to analyze the frequency spectra of 3-axis vibration data under different torque profiles. According to the experimental results, effective and reliable fault detection can be provided through frequency-related signals (fr (1X) and 2fr (2X)) and their sidebands (2fr+2sfs).

articleTitle: High Initial Acceleration Chest Compression Device
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The primary intervention in cardiac arrest is chest compression-based cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). While the American Heart Association (AHA) recommends standard manual CPR, various CPR devices have been developed to deliver more consistent compressions. However, clinical data suggest these devices do not improve survival rates as effectively as manual CPR. This may be because manual compressions produce higher initial momentum, making blood circulation more efficient. However, due to the limitations of piston technologies, current CPR devices cannot fully mimic this impulsive compression. In this study, a new CPR device that provides effective chest compressions with high initial acceleration thanks to the patented piston mechanism has been developed. The device's performance has been compared with the widely used LUCAS 3 device, and instantaneous acceleration data have been obtained through sensors integrated into the pistons of both devices. The results show that the developed device performs better in instantaneous acceleration and advances current mechanical CPR standards

articleTitle: Aktif Gürültü Kontrolü (ANC) Sisteminde Mikrofon ile Hoparlör Arasındaki Mesafenin Sistem Başarısına Etkisi
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Active Noise Control (ANC) systems have increasingly become a prominent solution for reducing in-vehicle noise. This study investigates the impact of the distance between the microphone and the speaker on the performance of ANC systems. The positioning within the vehicle is a critical factor that directly affects both the accurate detection of noise frequencies by the microphone and the effective propagation of the anti-noise signal. Experimental studies and simulations were conducted on a system built using the “Sigma Studio” software and Analog Devices “ADAU1467”DSP chip to analyze the noise cancellation performance as a function of varying the distance between the microphone and the speaker. The results demonstrate that optimizing this distance yields more efficient noise cancellation, particularly for low frequency noises. These findings emphasize the significance of microphone and speaker placement in the design of in-vehicle ANC systems and provide strategies for improving future system efficiency.

articleTitle: Life Cycle Assessment and Calculation of Carbon Footprint of PDU Systems Used in Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Nowadays data centers become more and more important. Increased number of data centers are built due to the emerging and expanding digital currency, IoT and AI applications. However, the share of data centers in the total world carbon footprint is skyrocketed due to demanded data volume. Energy consumption and material usage make the data centers prominent figures of CO2 emission sources. In this study, a Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and carbon footprint calculation method are implemented for rack-type PDUs (Power Distribution Unit) used in data centers. An excessive number of rack-type PDU systems used in data centers, even their share of carbon footprint is lesser in data center industry. The study also includes solutions and a road map for net zero carbon or de-carbonisation of PDUs.

articleTitle: Automated Separation of Caries Requiring Filling and Caries Requiring Root Canal from Full Dose and Low Dose Bitewing Images Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, an innovative computer-aided system based on deep learning has been developed for caries requiring filling and root canal treatment. With this system, dentists will be able to determine the type of caries in the tooth and decide on the appropriate treatment for the detected caries. Various variations with augmented 1250 bitewing images were used to automatically detect caries types in the first molar teeth. In the test phase, full-dose and low-dose versions of 84 bitewing images were used. The accuracy rates produced by the Detectron- 2 network in classifying caries types in fully dosed bitewing and low-dose bitewing images labeled by experienced dentists were observed as % 95.03 and 87.29 %, respectively. Success rates in distinguishing between canal and filling treatments for full-dose and low-dose imaging were observed as 88.09 % and 61.90 %, respectively. Additionally, the successful results of the network in low-dose images will also enable a reduction in the radiation level applied to patients. As a result, the proposed system has been successful in distinguishing teeth requiring canal and filling treatment.

articleTitle: Design of Artificial Electromagnetic Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents a novel polarization-insensitive metamaterial absorber based on a spherical unit cell. The performance of the absorber is evaluated using CST, a 3D full-wave electromagnetic simulation tool, under normal incidence for both TE and TM polarization modes. The spherical geometry of the unit cell allows the absorber to maintain approximately 90% stable absorption efficiency for both TE and TM modes within the 1-2.5 GHz frequency range. To improve absorption at lower incidence angles, a spherical cavity was introduced at the center of the unit cell, and surface-mount resistors (SMD) were positioned on top of the spherical structure. The spherical design was chosen because it offers the same surface area across all angles in spherical coordinates, enabling uniform absorption. The absorber is constructed using a plastic sphere with a radius of 60 mm and a thickness of 4 mm, featuring copper traces connected by SMD resistors. Our findings indicate that spherical-shaped metamaterials can provide superior absorption performance over a wide range of incident angles, making them highly effective for various electromagnetic applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approaches to Categorize Land-Use Types Using Building Electricity Consumption Data: Implementation and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This research presents an innovative machine learning approach for classifying land use types using building-level electricity consumption data. The main objective of the study is to categorize buildings into predetermined land use categories by analyzing electricity consumption patterns and subscriber information. The researchers have developed the model using advanced techniques such as XGBoost. This model has been tested in three pilot districts of Turkey (Karşıyaka, Çiğli, and Tepebaşı) with diverse urban structures. The model's performance has been evaluated using standard performance metrics such as precision and recall. Notably, ensemble learning methods (CatBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest) have consistently achieved high accuracy rates. A significant finding of this study is that electricity consumption data can be effective in classifying land use even in the absence of detailed municipal zoning data. This result is particularly important for regions where current or comprehensive zoning data is not available. The results of the research demonstrate that the use of machine learning techniques in the land-use analysis can provide significant improvements in the planning of electricity distribution networks and the project development of network investments. This approach can contribute to the development of more efficient and sustainable energy distribution systems.

articleTitle: Passive Radiometric Imaging System with Artificial Intelligence Based Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The Passive Radiometric Imaging System (PRIS), developed under TÜBİTAK MAM, stands out as a significant innovation in the field of security. This system detects natural Terahertz emissions radiating from the human body to identify objects concealed under clothing, such as explosive devices, firearms (pistols, rifles, knives), as well as illicit items like drugs, tobacco, meat, alcohol, and similar substances. PRIS converts these emissions into grayscale images, enabling the detection of objects without human intervention. In this study, instead of traditional image processing methods, artificial intelligence-based deep learning algorithms have been employed. These algorithms have achieved great success in object detection and tracking tasks, enhancing the system's accuracy and its capability to prevent security threats. Supported by deep learning techniques, PRIS facilitates faster and more reliable detection of potential threats, particularly in crowded areas, airports, and other critical security points. This approach aims to minimize security vulnerabilities and optimize preventive measures.

articleTitle: IEC61850 Based Integrated Protection Systems for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Connection of embedded generation units, energy storage systems and EVs into distribution networks provide several benefits from the view point of environmental conditions, power producers and customers, however create several technical problems for the protection and control of the distribution networks. Developments in the computer and data communications technologies create several opportunities to overcome these technical difficulties. This paper will discuss the present applications and future suggestions of IEC 61850 communications protocols in the field of protection and control. Integrated protection systems using IEC61850 protocol, its applications and future suggestions will be considered for the protection of microgrids. In particular, The Integrated Protection Systems developed using IEC61850 technologies, their applications and forward-looking thoughts in the protection of microgrids will be discussed

articleTitle: Multi-Lane Detection System using Perspective Transform and Curve Fitting for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study presents a multi-lane detection system designed to accurately identify road lanes for autonomous vehicles. In the proposed system, perspective transformation and curve fitting techniques are applied to the images obtained from the vehicle's camera to detect lane markings. The lane detection results obtained from the YOLOPv2 model are further refined through contour detection and polynomial curve fitting processes, ensuring precise lane modeling. The system was tested on both straight and curved roads, achieving successful results in both scenarios. In future work, new tests and algorithm improvements will be conducted to enhance the performance under different road conditions and environmental factors. Additionally, future efforts will focus on detecting various lane types such as emergency lanes and side road connections.

articleTitle: A Digital Clock that Can Also Be Used by a Blind Person
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this project, a digital clock application with auditory feedback capabilities has been developed for visually impaired individuals. STM32G030C8T6 was used as the controller in the hardware of the system. Additionally, a 20×4 LCD is employed for visual output. The STM32 microcontroller's internal clock module provides real-time data which is displayed on the LCD. The user can access features such as getting real time and date as audio feedback, time setting, alarm functionality, voice recording, alarm sound selection, and volume control through buttons and a menu interface. A distinctive feature of the system is its ability to record up to two 30-second alarm sounds, elevating the product beyond a conventional clock by enhancing its utility in daily life. A user-friendly box design was created using a 3D modeling environment, with special consideration for the target users. The buttons and switches are equipped with Braille, making the device more accessible for visually impaired users.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for STEMI and NSTEMI Diagnosis Using Empirical Wavelet Transform of Multi-Lead ECG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Today, with technological advancements, numerous computer- aided systems are being developed for diagnosing heart diseases using Electrocardiography (ECG) signals. Myocardial infarction (MI), a cardiovascular disease, occurs due to insufficient blood supply or blockage of blood flow to the heart. Analyzing ECG signals is crucial for the early diagnosis of MI. In this study, a novel approach involving feature extraction and machine learning algorithms is proposed to classify different MI conditions (STEMI, NSTEMI) with a healthy control (HC) group using 12-lead ECG signals. In the proposed method, after preprocessing the 12-channel ECG signals, a classification study was conducted using features extracted from sub-band signals obtained via Empirical Wavelet Transform, classifying the groups into HC-NSTEMI, HC-STEMI, HC-NSTEMI-STEMI, and NSTEMI-STEMI. According to the results, the HC-STEMI group was classified with the highest performance, achieving an AUC of 0.996 using Artificial Neural Networks through 5-fold cross-validation. In conclusion, this study demonstrates the significant potential of multi-channel ECG signal analysis for MI diagnosis, contributing to future studies in this field..

articleTitle: Increasing Average Output Power by using a Fuzzy Logic Based Maximum Power Point Tracking Method in Wind Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In solar and wind power plants, it is desired that the power generated is always maximum. However, changes in the input parameters of the system may prevent this. Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods can be used especially in solar power plants. In wind power plants, speed and direction of the wind are always variable. As in solar power plants, instantaneous/average power amounts can be increased in wind power plants by using MPPT methods. In this study, Incremental Conductance, Perturb and Observe, Fuzzy Logic and models created without using any MPPT method were used. The average power values obtained by performing MATLAB/Simulink simulations were compared for the relevant scenarios. According to the results, it is seen that the output power can be increased by using MPPT methods. The highest increase was obtained by using Fuzzy Logic-based method. This is a beneficial result in terms of grid operation and energy planning.

articleTitle: PIλDμ Approach for High-Efficiency BLDC Motor Control
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, we present the design and implementation of a Fractional-Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative (FOPID), also known as PI<sup>λ</sup>D<sup>μ</sup> speed controller for Brushless DC (BLDC) motors. BLDC motors are widely used in various applications due to their high efficiency and performance. However, effective control of BLDC motors remains a challenging task due to nonlinear properties and variable operating conditions. Results show that FOPID demonstrates significantly outperform; their integer-order counterpart on performance criteria such as overshooting, rise time, transient duration, and undershoot, due to the inherent flexibility of the volume distribution.

articleTitle: A New Location Estimation Error Minimization Model Based on Wi-Fi and Mobile Phone for Indoor Mobile Nodes Considering Human Population
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Nowadays, emerging needs and solutions driven by the fact that most of the people in active socio-economic life spend their time indoors have increased the importance of indoor positioning methods and their use in navigation technologies. Since traditional global navigation satellite systems do not work effectively, radio frequency based technologies such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID and UWB are preferred for indoor positioning. With its high potential for widespread use, Wi-Fi signals offer highly accurate positioning in a wide range of applications without requiring any additional hardware in existing WLAN infrastructures. In the new model presented in this paper, we propose a new approach for Wi-Fi based indoor positioning solutions by analyzing the effects of human presence, mobility and other relevant dynamic factors to improve the accuracy of precise location estimation, especially making use of instantaneous data from specific mobile phone sensors.

articleTitle: On the Performance of NOMA-Based Cooperative Communication Systems with Best Relay Selection over Nakagami-m fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Cooperative communications systems with best relay selection provide antenna diversity gain by constituting virtual antenna arrays in the wireless network. On the other hand, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique has been proposed to achieve improved user access in the fifth generation (5G) wireless communications. The combination of the NOMA approach and the cooperative communications with best relay selection technique will play an important role in providing the service quality required by the new generation radio communication technologies. In this study, the performance of NOMA based cooperative communications with best relay seleciton is investigated over the Nakagami-m fading channels by providing computer simulation results for the achievable average rate. The obtained results have shown that the capacity is increased as the fading parameter m or the number of total relays increase.

articleTitle: 1500VDA Bataryalı Enerji Depolama Sistemi Uygulamalarında Kullanılan 200kW Çift Yönlü Güç Dönüştürücüler için İki ve Üç Düzeyli Topolojilerde Elektro-Isıl Çözümleme Çalışması
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of power semiconductor technology, SiC MOSFETs have attracted great attention in a wide range of applications in the power electronics industry. In this paper, two different design comparisons based on two-level SiC MOSFET and three-level Active-Neutral-Point-Clamped (ANPC) Si IGBTs have been performed for a grid-connected, bidirectional power flow converter with a nominal power of200 kW, used in battery energy storage system (BESS) applications. Sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) has been used as a modulation type. The power losses, efficiency and temperature values of the semiconductors in the two designs have been compared by means of PLECS simulation program.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fuel Cell System Power Using Fuzzy Logic Based PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study aims to develop an optimized power control strategy for fuel cell systems. The strategy focuses on adjusting the system's net power using a classical feedback controller while optimizing the oxygen excess ratio (λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub>). Ensuring the optimal λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub> value is essential in all operating conditions to avoid performance degradation due to oxygen deficiency and to prevent unnecessary energy consumption caused by excess oxygen. A data-driven reference generator is designed to produce the optimal λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub> reference value. A fuzzy logic based PID controller, offering flexibility for nonlinear system dynamics, is used for λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub> control. Additionally, a feedforward controller is added in λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub> control to reduce the coupling effect related net power. The proposed control strategy was tested on an open-source fuel cell model, achieving a decoupling effect on λ<sub>o</sub><sub>2</sub> response with negligible impact on power performance. The effectiveness of strategy was further validated using a model-derived efficiency expression

articleTitle: A Resonator Design for Mutual Coupling Reduction Between Microstrip Antennas in MIMO Applications at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: A simple resonator structure is proposed to reduce the mutual coupling between rectangular microstrip patch antennas positioned close to each other for MIMO applications at 28 GHz center frequency. Here, the frequency of 28 GHz is chosen because it is one of middle bands for 5G communication in USA. Two microstrip patch antennas with gaps using a common dielectric substrate and a ground plane are employed as antennas and the patches are closely placed with an edge-to-edge distance of 0.6 mm (approximately λ/18). In order to reduce the mutual coupling between these radiating elements and increase the isolation, a resonator is positioned between them and its parameters are optimized. In the simulations, it is observed that the proposed resonator reduces the coupling by approximately 10 dB. By this result, it can be concluded that the proposed structure may be suitable for tightly packed MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Optical Communication Channels between Earth and Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Due to the development of technology, the need for long-distance communication is increasing rapidly day by day. Communication across long distances by integrating wired and wireless communications is becoming widespread. In this study, communication between the earth and satellites and communication between satellites in different orbits were analyzed. In the setups modeled with the OptiSystem 7.0 simulation program, a free space optical (FSO) communication structure was designed for the communication systems in question, where CSRZ (Carrier Suppressed Return to Zero) and NRZ (Non-Return to Zero) advanced modulation formats were used. In two bidirectional inter-satellite communication lines between the earth, LEO (Low Earth Orbit) and GEO (Geostationary Earth Orbit), WSS (Wavelength Selecter Switch) and add-drop structure were used.

articleTitle: Federated Learning Application in Human Activity Recognition: The Impact of Aggregation Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In recently, Human Activity Recognition studies occupy an important place among artificial intelligence problems. Although many successful results have been achieved in numerous studies conducted in this field, data privacy is often overlooked. In this presented study, a Federated Learning application, which prioritizes data privacy, has been used to solve the Human Activity Recognition problem. In this context, a study has been conducted in which four different strategies were tested and the Transformers architecture was used as a model. When the obtained results were examined, it was observed that the Federated Loss-Based Coefficients method, which produced successful results especially in heterogeneous data sets, achieved an average of 96.08% success, obtaining better results compared to other aggregation functions.

articleTitle: Improving Human-Like Driving Behavior in Autonomous Vehicles with Deep Reinforcement Learning and Action Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the objective is to develop human-like driving behaviors in autonomous vehicles using a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework. Visual feature extraction and dimensionality reduction from RGB camera images are conducted using an autoencoder, which allows the agent to analyze the driving environment more effectively. Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm is selected as the DRL method for decision-making and control in autonomous driving; additionally, action noise is incorporated to facilitate a more efficient learning process. Action filtering techniques, such as Exponential Moving Average (EMA) and Weighted Moving Average (WMA), are employed to smooth the movements of the steering and throttle, thereby enhancing driving fluidity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully establishes a balance between exploration and exploitation, promising a human-like and seamless autonomous driving experience.

articleTitle: CKKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption Based Comparison and Bitonic Sorting
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the increasing importance of data security, fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enabling privacy-preserving processing has come to the forefront. This study addresses the privacy-preserving sorting problem using FHE. Due to the nature of FHE, conventional sorting algorithms cannot be directly applied, necessitating the use of data-independent algorithms such as the Bitonic Sort Network. In the literature, Bitonic Sort networks based on CKKS perform the comparison operation through scheme switching. In this study, however, the Bitonic Sort Network comparison operation is implemented and its performance is analyzed analyzed using the CKKS scheme and the OpenFHE library. The challenges of the comparison operation within FHE are discussed, and different comparison methods are examined. The findings obtained will pave the way for the development of new high-performance sorting algorithms based on CKKS.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Segmentation in Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: 3D segmentation methods can be applied to the segmentation studies of large scale point cloud data in urban areas. In this study, point cloud segmentation was carried out for three big Chinese cities, nanemly Chengdu, Jiaoda, Shenzhen. Due to not having enough labelled data from these urban areas for model training, transfer learning techniques were adapted using SensatUrban and Toronto-3D datasets. Experimental results show that proposed method enables achieving F1 scores above 80% for each region. Transfer learning strategy offers a reliable solution to overcome the problem of labelled dataset scarcity for the task of 3D point cloud segmentation in urban areas. The findings also contribute to the advancement of point cloud segmentation methods, particularly in the context of rapidly developing Chinese urban areas.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of LSTM-Capsule Networks and 3DConv-LSTM Autoencoder in Ambient Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Considering the population density in cities, manual detection of abnormal situations in the ambient by humans is an economically expensive and time-consuming application. In recent years, a number of approaches have been proposed for anomaly detection. Compared to other approaches, deep learning models have achieved great accuracy in detecting a wide variety of abnormal events. The unsupervised models outperform other deep learning models in anomaly detection. Therefore, in this study, two unsupervised deep learning models (LSTM-Capsule Networks and 3DConv-LSTMAutoencoder) are compared and analyzed with each other in the feature extraction stage. Performance is evaluated with accuracy and loss metrics. The Python programming language is used. And this work is tested with ambient anomaly datasets such as CUHK Avenue, UCSD Ped1, and UCSD Ped2. The experimental results showed that LSTM-Capsule Networks outperform the 3DConv-LSTM Autoencoder and have high potential in ambient anomaly detection among the existing methods we examined.

articleTitle: Design of a Broadband Metamaterial Solar Cell with Hilbert Fractal Geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study a three-layered metamaterial absorber solar cell, which has a broadband high absorption rate, is designed aiming to contribute to renewable energy production and enhance the efficiency of standard solar cells. The optical properties of the design were analyzed using numerical methods. It has been observed that the designed metamaterial solar cell has absorption rate exceeding 86% in the 100 - 1000 THz frequency range. The obtained absorption data were combined with photovoltaic parameter calculations under AM1.5 spectrum standards, resulting in a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 59.69 mA/cm<sup>2</sup> and an efficiency (η) of 33.66%. It has been demonstrated that this design possesses significant potential for solar energy applications due to its high efficiency, environmentally friendly characteristics, and cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Design of a Wireless Battery Management System for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on a Wi-Fi and BLE Module
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a wireless battery management system (wBMS) design is presented for use in the management of lithium-ion batteries. The designed system was developed to perform critical functions such as cell balancing, data transmission, and the safe monitoring of batteries. Thanks to the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) modules used in the system, the battery status can be wirelessly monitored, and data transmission can be achieved. It is aimed to extend battery life by monitoring cell balancing algorithms and parameters such as the temperature and voltage of the batteries. The wireless data transmission performance and cell balancing results of the design were analyzed, and the reliability and efficiency of the system were evaluated based on the obtained data.

articleTitle: Disease Classification in Retinal Images Using Vision Transformer and Capsule Network
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Disease classification in retinal image analysis is of great importance in terms of accelerating the diagnostic process and increasing its accuracy in ophthalmology. Early diagnosis of retinal diseases plays a critical role in preventing the progression of diseases and managing treatment processes more effectively. Deep learning classification models offer an innovative and effective solution for the diagnosis of retinal diseases. In this study, a hybrid model combining Vision Transformer and Capsule Network is proposed. Vision Transformer provides in-depth extraction of visual features. Capsule Network increases the classification success by preserving the spatial relationships of these features. In experiments using RFMiD dataset, the performance of the proposed model is compared with VGG-16, VGG-19, Xception and ViT models. The experimental results show that the model improves the classification accuracy. The findings of the study show that new methods can be effective in computer-aided diagnosis of retinal diseases.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna Designs for WiFi/Bluetooth and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, four microstrip patch antenna designs that can be used in WiFi/Bluetooth and 5G applications are presented. By designing an antenna structure and changing the feed point, antennas suitable for different applications are obtained. 50 ohm coaxial feed is used as the feed structure. The antenna stands out with its unique geometry, light weight and low profile, as well as easy integration.

articleTitle: Effect of Element Number and Bending Angle on Conformal Array Antenna Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the effect of changing the array bending angle and the number of array elements on the array radiation pattern was examined for the case where the conformal array antenna radiates through boresight and phase compensation is provided. In the radiation pattern analysis, comparisons were made by taking into account the change in 3 dB and 10 dB beam width values.

articleTitle: Using Heuristic Algorithms in the Placement of Capacitors and Distributed Generation Systems to Reduce Losses and Voltage Variations in Energy Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Nowadays, continuous studies are carried out for the development and improvement of electricity distribution networks. In order to minimize the losses in distribution networks and to reduce the voltage drops, distributed generation systems (DG) and capacitors are placed in the distribution system. In this study, the optimum positions and capacities of DGs and capacitors to be placed in the distribution network were determined in order to reduce the network losses in the distribution system and the voltage deviation of the system. For this purpose, heuristic optimization algorithms such as PSO, ABC and SFS were used. The proposed method was programmed in MATLAB and tested in a 34-bus standard IEEE distribution system. The results show that the optimum distribution of DGs or capacitors with equal total capacities to two different buses rather than connecting them to one bus affects the system more positively. By using these algorithms, a decrease of up to 36.66% in the active power loss and 31.36% in the voltage deviation of the system after the placement of the capacitor and DG was achieved. Although the algorithms give similar results, it is understood that SFS can be more successful than other algorithms with the best starting value and fewer iterations.

articleTitle: Reducing the Number of Scenarios in Automated Driving Systems: Methods and Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study focuses on reducing the number of scenarios in scenario-based testing processes for AD systems. Due to the complexity of AD systems, traditional distance-based testing methods prove insufficient, making scenario-based testing a more efficient solution. The study examines methods such as parameter elimination, boundary narrowing, and optimization/searching to reduce and optimize the number of test scenarios. These approaches aim to streamline testing by reducing costs and time while ensuring the safety validation of AD systems. Through the proposed strategies, non-critical scenarios can be filtered out, and critical scenarios can be prioritized for testing

articleTitle: Fracture Detection with Different Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Fractures or injuries occurring in bones negatively impact daily life and activities. Fractures or injuries are frequently observed in bones located close to the skin surface, which necessitates rapid detection and accurate treatment. This study focuses on methods for quickly and easily detecting fractures in bones close to the surface, such as the tibia. A Vivaldi antenna operating in the high-frequency range of 10.5�13.5 GHz was used for fast and easy detection. An electromagnetic measurement simulation environment was created using CST Microwave Studio�, where the anatomy of the tibial bone tissue�including bone marrow, spongy bone, and cortical bone�was represented in detail through precise geometry. Comparative simulation results were obtained for antenna array methods with the proposed antenna, allowing for rapid and highly accurate detection of bone fractures, and its effectiveness in fracture detection was analyzed.

articleTitle: Detection of Poisonous Substances in Their Water Solutions by Using Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a non-invasive method is presented for the detection of toxic substances in water by measuring the transmission coefficient (including amplitude and phase values) of electromagnetic waves through a dielectric waveguide surrounding a liquid-filled container. Electromagnetic waves in two different frequency ranges, 75-110 GHz and 90-140 GHz, interact with the liquid as they propagate through the waveguide and radiate into the external environment. The study tested various dissolved toxic substances in water using both plastic and glass containers. It was observed that the spectral transmission properties of these toxic substances are significantly different from water, especially when using millimeter waves. These differences in transmission characteristics were analyzed using machine learning algorithms such as k-means clustering and principal component analysis (PCA), effectively distinguishing between hazardous substances and water. This approach provides a very fast and reliable method for the quick and immediate detection of hazardous substances in water. This study also offers a potential method for applications in environmental monitoring and public health, such as safety assessments of drinking water.

articleTitle: Quadcopter Altitude Control Using Classical PID and Cascaded PID with Adaptive Feedforward Extension
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is modeled, and then classical PID and adaptive feedforward cascade PID controllers are designed for altitude control. The performance analysis of these controller structures, while the quadcopter UAV performed point tracking and level flight tasks, is conducted according to error metrics the integral of squared error (ISE), the integral of time-weighted squared error (ITSE), the integral of absolute error (IAE), and the integral of time- weighted absolute error (ITAE. The performance of the designed controllers is evaluated with simulations carried out in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. As a result, it is observed that the cascade PID controller increased the performance by an average of 32.6% during the point tracking task, while the adaptive feedforward cascade PID controller demonstrated better performance in terms of error metrics during level flight.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Number of Elements on Leakage Currents in Iced String Insulators
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: String insulators are of critical importance for the insulation and safety of electrical transmission and distribution lines. In regions where winter conditions are intense, the icing factor negatively affects the performance of string insulators. Icing reduces the resistance of the insulator surface and reduces the insulation property, resulting in an increase in leakage currents. This situation poses a danger for the continuity of transmission and distribution lines by causing insulator damage. In this study, the analysis of leakage currents of iced porcelain string insulators according to the number of elements was performed. An alternating voltage of 20 kV was applied to the ıced string insulators; leakage currents were obtained with the help of the LabVIEW program, and the effect of the number of elements of the string insulator on leakage currents was compared using experimental data. The relationship between the number of elements of the insulators and the number of leakage current pulses was examined.

articleTitle: Implementation of the YOLOv8 Convolutional Neural Network Block on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Hardware implementation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), a key AI topic recently, is as important as the algorithm itself. The computational intensity, reaching millions of operations, has driven efforts to enhance speed, energy efficiency, and resource use. Based on this, we designed and implemented the first layer (16 channels) of the YOLOv8n object tracking algorithm on an FPGA using various hardware architectures. For this purpose, we utilized parallelism, pipelining techniques, and hard-wired block RAMs. We designed ten different CNN IP cores using VHDL. We tested the system containing each IP structure at 100-150 MHz and the IP cores themselves at 200-250 MHz. In these tests, we processed a 640x640x3 image through 16 filters of 3x3x3 size. Our design, taking only 0.141 seconds, operates 648 times faster than an ARM A9 processor embedded in the FPGA, and 2.8 times faster than a PC with an i7-6700HQ CPU and 8GB of RAM.

articleTitle: Effects of Brush Shift on Performance and Experimental Verification of Direct Current Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of brush shifting method is examined to improve the performance of brushed DC motors used in automatic door systems. The brush angles were tested to reduce commutation problems caused by armature reaction and to enhance motor efficiency. In the experiments, the motor was operated under nominal load, and current waveforms obtained by shifting the brushes clockwise (CW) and counterclockwise (CCW) at 4° and 8° angles were analyzed. The results show that shifting the brushes 4° in the counterclockwise direction minimizes current ripple and significantly reduces arcing during commutation. This method offers an effective solution to increase motor efficiency and reduce energy losses.

articleTitle: Different Capacitance Multiplier Structures With Noise Analyses For Low Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, comprehensive analyses of two different capacitance multiplier structures have been conducted, and noise optimization strategies have been discussed. There are two different capacitance multiplier structures to be analyzed in terms of noise in this study. The capacitance multiplier structures analyzed for noise are the Multi-Output Voltage Differencing Transconductance Amplifier (MO-VDTA) based capacitance multiplier structures and the Multi-Output Current Differencing Transconductance Amplifier (MO-CDTA) based capacitance multiplier structures. In the MO-VDTA based capacitance multiplier structure, the multiplication factor varies between 120 and 750 depending on the .... current value. Additionally, the cutoff frequency of the second-order low-pass filter implemented with this structure ranges from 2 kHz to 12.4 kHz. The other capacitance multiplier analyzed for noise is the MO-CDTA based capacitance multiplier structure. In this structure, the multiplication factor k varies between 400 and 1250 by changing the ...... voltage of the external PMOS connected to the Z terminal. The MO-CDTA structure has been used in the second order low-pass filter, and it has been observed that the cutoff frequency varies between 23.6 kHz and 91 kHz with the change in the multiplication factor k. Comprehensive noise analyses of the filter applications of the two structures mentioned in this study have been examined

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Patch Antennas with Rectangular Slots for Laminate and Wearable Materials at 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, new multi-band patch antenna design models are proposed for use in 5G networks. The purpose of the designs is to open rectangular slots on rectangular shaped patch antennas and bring them to the desired operating conditions with parametric analyzes. The designs were carried out by following the same procedure steps using five different dielectric laminate substrate materials, such as RO3003, RT6006, FR4, RO3203, RO6010, and one denim fabric base material. The antennas were compared in terms of return loss, gain and radiation characteristics. Except for the antenna designed with RO3203 at certain values of rectangular slots, radiation at multiple frequencies was obtained at 5G frequencies. With the proposed method, improvement was observed for return loss and bandwidth characteristics in the RO3203 based antenna. This study will be a resource for antenna researchers by revealing the responses of different substrate materials to the same design method for 5G bands in patch antennas.

articleTitle: An Application of Prosumer Electric Load Forecasting with Machine Learning-Based Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Latterly, the concept of prosumer has been commonly used with the ascending penetration of renewable energy sources into current power distribution networks. The consumer term in electricity markets has been evolved into prosumer which can be defined as an individual who consumes and produces electricity. Considering the rising demand for energy, the research of prosumer electric load forecasting has become crucial for maintaining the stability of distribution networks. The prevalent utilisation of machine learning-based methods in electric load forecasting studies demonstrates the efficacy of these approaches in the field of forecasting. This study aims to forecast quarter hour-ahead prosumer net metering consumption using a household dataset from Austin, Texas, USA with the employment of gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks and extreme gradient boosted decision trees (XGBoost) algorithms. Consequently, the results of the study demonstrated that utilising XGBoost algorithm outperformed the GRU networks algorithm for prosumer electric load forecasting in terms of coefficient of determination (R<sup>2</sup>) and root mean squared error (RMSE) by 90.36% and 0.498 kWh, respectively. Furthermore, it is considered that literature for prosumer electric load forecasting has not been adequately articulated and this paper will not only provide guidance for the young researchers in the field, but also bridge this gap.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Gysel Power Divider for 915 MHz ISM Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Power dividers and combiners play a critical role in modern wireless communication systems, particularly in RF power amplifier applications and antenna arrays. These components are crucial for dividing and combining signals in an equal-phase and equal-amplitude manner, enabling the achievement of higher power levels. This study presents the design of a Gysel Power Divider operating at a center frequency of 915 MHz. The design is optimized through adjustments to the dimensions of microstrip lines, with geometric arrangements implemented to minimize physical size.
