Successful results were obtained from electromagnetic simulations, leading to the production of a prototype and subsequent experimental tests. The measurement results are presented in comparison with simulation data, and the performance of the circuit is analyzed. This work details the design of a Gysel Power Divider developed for high-power industrial, scientific, and medical applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Large Language Models on Turkish Question-Answer Texts
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: One of the most studied topics in the field of natural language processing is question-answering systems. In recent years, finding the answer to a question asked within a given text has become increasingly important. In this study, a fine-tuning process was conducted on large language models using the SQuAD 1.1 dataset containing Turkish historical data. Five different large language models were fine-tuned in this study: "bert-base-uncased", "bert-base-turkish-cased", "distilbert- base-multilingual-cased", "mt5-base", and "mBart-large-50". While BERT and DistilBERT models use only the encoder part of the Transformer architecture, models like mT5 and mBART use both the encoder and decoder. It was ensured that most of the selected models were multilingual. Additionally, the performance of the non-multilingual "bert-base-uncased " model on Turkish data was also examined. To evaluate the study results, EM, F1, and Rouge metrics were used. As a result of the study, the "mBART" model achieved better results compared to the other models.

articleTitle: Development of a Real-Time Data-Supported Energy Consumption Model for Electric Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)

articleTitle: Stock Price Prediction Using Mamba
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The prices in the stock market constantly fluctuate due to the influence of internal and external dynamics. For investors, predicting these movements can provide a significant advantage. Accurately forecasting stock prices is crucial for both reducing investment risks and increasing returns, while preventing financial losses. However, the volatile and complex nature of financial markets makes this process challenging. Recently, models like Mamba, based on state space models, have delivered effective results in sequence modelling. In this study, the goal was to predict stock closing prices using the Mamba model. The model's performance was evaluated on the prices of six companies listed on the Nasdaq. Mamba demonstrated better performance with lower error rates compared to our baseline models, MLP and LSTM. These results may help investors reduce risks and make more informed decisions.

articleTitle: Material Selection in Transformer Core Design for Cost and Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Transformers play a vital role in power distribution and efficiency; selecting the correct core material is essential for optimizing performance and cost. This study examines the economic and efficiency aspects of two mostly used cold-rolled grain-oriented electrical steels, H0 and M4. Transformers are designed according to the TEDAŞ MLZ Specifications. This study not only accounts for the material costs associated with H0 and M4 but also highlights additional expenses, including processing and manufacturing costs. The study also compares the no-load losses and the weight of the cores. Understanding the economic and efficiency aspects of material selection can lead to optimized designs that enhance both performance and cost efficiency. To validate no-load losses, no-load losses are also calculated using finite element models of the transformers. This study aims to empower transformer designers and power suppliers to make more strategic material choices based on economic conditions, ultimately leading to optimized transformer designs.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance and Efficiency Analysis of Conventional and Active Clamp Forward Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The increasing demand for energy has made the efficient and sustainable use of power sources increasingly popular. Due to their high efficiency, switch-mode power supplies (SMPS) are often preferred over linear power supplies. However, the losses occurring in these converters lead to an increase in the junction temperature of semiconductor components, which affects their operational lifespan. Among SMPS, forward converters are widely used, especially in low- and medium-power applications requiring isolation. In this study, the thermal analysis of conventional and active-clamp forward converters was conducted using the PLECS software. It was found that the active-clamp topology reduces power losses by 44.9% and lowers junction temperature by 27.7%. Consequently, the active-clamp forward converter demonstrates superior performance in terms of efficiency and reliability compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: Determination of Optimal Component Values in Low-Pass Filter Design Using Red Fox Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the optimization of sixth-order Butterworth low- pass filter components was performed using the recently introduced Red Fox Optimization (RFO) algorithm in the literature. The RFO is a meta-heuristic optimization method inspired by nature, specifically modeling the hunting strategies of foxes. The primary objective of RFO is to optimize the search process effectively, enabling the attainment of optimal results. In this study, the RFO algorithm was implemented in MATLAB to optimize the resistance and capacitance values required for the low-pass filter, taking into account the specified cutoff frequency and quality factors. The E24 industrial series was employed to realize the optimized filter components. To validate the accuracy of the optimized results, the obtained values were simulated and analyzed using LTSpice. The simulations demonstrated that the RFO algorithm achieved an error rate of 0.0113 in the optimal filter design, and these findings were compared with those reported in the literature.

articleTitle: An Effective Parallel-Plate MEMS Capacitor Design for Energy HarvestingApplications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study presents an innovative micro electrostatic energy harvester system capable of harvesting energy from ultrasonic waves. This unique design, utilizing parallel plate capacitors, aims to meet the increasing demand for self-sustaining energy systems in areas such as wearable technology and biomedical electronics.Unlike conventional energy harvesters, our system significantly increases energy conversion efficiency by leveraging an optimized parallel plate capacitor configuration. This approach enables us to achieve high performance in microelectronic and MEMS systems, particularly in the mentioned application areas, by minimizing energy loss. Our system demonstrates a notable increase in efficiency, especially in low-frequency and low-amplitude energy sources. This feature enables effective energy harvesting even from low-energy sources such as body movements. This technology not only contributes to the development of more reliable and autonomously operating devices but also opens new horizons for sustainable energy solutions in ultrasonic wave-based technologies. Our research takes an important step in the fields of energy efficiency and sustainability by paving the way for future self-sustaining electronic devices.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Economic Feasibility of Different Materials for Transformer Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Power transformers play a crucial role in the transmission and distribution of electrical power, ensuring that energy reaches consumers efficiently and reliably. The selection of winding material is a key factor that significantly influences both the performance and overall cost of a power transformer. This study conducts a thorough price comparison between aluminum and copper used in transformer windings. The economic factors of both materials, including their costs and core weights, are compared. Transformers analyzed in this research are designed in accordance with Turkey's MLZ standard. The results offer valuable insights into the relative costs and trade-offs of each material in transformer manufacturing. By understanding these costs, manufacturers, researchers, and power providers can make better decisions about material selection, striking a balance between price and performance to optimize transformer design and efficiency in electrical power systems. The insights derived from this research can contribute to more sustainable practices in transformer production, supporting the ongoing evolution of energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Root Cause Analysis of Monitor Performance Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Vehicle software includes functions specific to the On-Board Diagnostic System (OBD) in order to monitor the performance of manufactured vehicles and detect in-vehicle faults and regulations use In-Use Monitor Performance Ratio (IUMPR) to monitor the performance of these systems. In the American and European markets, it is a requirement during vehicle operation that the IUMPR remains above certain limits. For this reason, engineers perform many driving tests and evaluate the results to observe how the calibrations affect vehicle performance. When the results are below the limits, root cause analysis is performed using software documentations. In this study, IUMPR root cause analysis is performed quickly and automatically by using machine learning techniques. Two different vehicle datasets were analyzed using supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods. The root causes obtained as a result of the analysis performed by engineers confirm the root causes obtained using machine learning.

articleTitle: Accurate Transient Voltage Protection and Circuit Simulation for Analog Circuits With Memristors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This work focuses on utilizing memristors as protection components against voltage transients in analog integrated circuits. It is shown that memristors provide more precise protection compared to protection measures implemented with discrete components and take up less space. The proposed usage method, along with the designed circuits and the circuit simulations created for using memristors as protection elements, is demonstrated. To ensure protection, Transient Voltage Suppression (TVS) diodes will also be used as the initial protection component.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient and Low-Complexity Spatial Modulation System with Deep Neural Network-Based Capacity-Optimized Antenna Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this paper, a new telecommunication system with high data rate, energy efficiency, and low complexity is proposed by combining COAS and spatial modulation (SM) using a DNN. The proposed technique is the integration of DNN, COAS and SM and is referred to as DNN-COAS-SM (DCS). Spatial modulation improves data transmission efficiency by encoding additional information using the indices of active antennas. The proposed DCS system improves system performance and reduces complexity by using a DNN-based COAS technique to optimize antenna selections. The integration of DNN into the antenna selection process improves the speed of decision-making, ensuring high performance even in complex communication environments. Evaluated in Rayleigh fading channels using M-QAM, this system shows improvement in bit error rate performance compared to conventional SM systems. Moreover, since DCS is DNN-based, the proposed system requires less computational overhead than conventional COAS systems

articleTitle: Investigation into the Performance of Impedance-Based Fault Location Algorithms in Medium Voltage Distribution Networks using COMTRADE Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Except for large metropolitan cities, medium voltage distribution networks have a high percentage of overhead lines. Overhead lines are one of the network elements with the highest number of fault occurrences. Besides, distribution networks have many laterals and branches. This topological structure of the distribution network creates difficulties, especially in locating single-phase ground faults. Many methods proposed in the literature require additional devices that are quite difficult to apply in the field or are expensive. In this study, two different impedance-based fault location algorithms were applied to COMTRADE data obtained from existing protection relays in the field. Both algorithms gave similar results and successfully detected the location of the single phase ground fault occurring in the field without requiring an additional measurement setup.

articleTitle: Asenkron Motorlarda Besleme Gerilimi Değişiminin Temel Parametreler Üzerindeki Etkisi
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the effect of parameter variation for 50% below and 50% above the nominal voltage of an induction motor is investigated. The values 50% below and 50% above the nominal voltage of 400 V are given as 200 volts and 600 volts For these ranges of values, a comprehensive set of parameters is analyzed and the effect of voltage variations on the parameters is given graphically. This study provides valuable insights into the parameter variation between supply voltage and motor performance. The effects of the parameters against voltage variation and their causes contribute to a better understanding of induction motor behavior and support the development of optimized motor designs and control strategies for real practical applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Voltage-Based Algorithm for Parallel Connection of Uninterruptible Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a voltage-based method is proposed for parallel connection of uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). In the proposed method, UPSs with the same power can be connected in parallel and power can be increased, resulting in a high-power system. The developed method ensures balanced power sharing between parallel UPSs. Synchronization information is sent analogue between parallel UPSs, UPS load percentage, DC bus voltage values, modulation index and other critical information are transmitted via CAN communication. To verify the proposed parallelization method, three UPSs of 160kVA power are connected in parallel. The PSIM simulation program is used to obtain the output voltage and current waveforms of the UPSs under different operating conditions. In the simulation environment, it is observed that the output voltage is stable and balanced current sharing is performed.

articleTitle: Real-Time Localization Application of MEKF-VDPL Algorithm on Autonomous Wheelchair in a Dynamic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The problem of determining the location of a mobile robot while moving is called the localization problem in autonomy. During navigation, it is vital to obtain high accuracy information about where the mobile robot is on the global coordinate system so that it can reach a predetermined goal smoothly and safely without hitting obstacles. For this reason, there has been an increased focus on localization in recent years with the aim of designing algorithms that can make both faster and more accurate position estimation. In this study, the MEKF-VDPL (Modified Extended Kalman Filter using Virtual Dynamic Point Landmark) localization algorithm, which was designed in MATLAB and has been introduced to the literature recently, has been made available on a wheelchair for the first time in real time, and real-time localization tests of this algorithm have been performed using a test scenario closer to the real-world dynamic environment. The localization test of the AMCL (Adaptive Monte Carlo Localization) algorithm has been also performed with the same test scenario. When the results obtained are compared, it is understood that the MEKF-VDPL localization algorithm has both faster and more accurate performance results.

articleTitle: Classification of Plant Leaf Diseases Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Study of Various Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Plant disease classification is an important task to increase agricultural sustainability and productivity. This study conducted a comparative analysis of deep neural networks DenseNet, ResNet, and GoogleNet for automatic classification of plant diseases. Data from 19 disease classes including Apple Black Rot, Potato Early Blight, and Tomato Late Blight were used in the study. DenseNet achieved the highest accuracy (99.80%) on the test data, outperforming ResNet (98.95%) and GoogleNet (98.30%) for efficiently extracting complex features. Data augmentation techniques improved the robustness of the models to changing research conditions. The results highlight the potential of DenseNet for diagnostic automation and integration into mobile and drone systems. In the future, it is planned to expand the dataset and use adaptation methods to various conditions.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Energy Management in Networked Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Networked microgrids are energy systems where multiple microgrids are interconnected and operate together. Networked microgrids provide operational flexibility by enabling the effective integration of distributed energy resources. The control methods used in these systems play a critical role in the dynamic performance, stability, and reliability of the grid, as well as provide advantages in terms of energy cost. This study evaluates the technical and economic advantages and disadvantages of centralized and decentralized control methods in microgrids, integrating operational constraints, technical constraints, line losses, and load flow, and assessing the impacts of both approaches on microgrid performance.

articleTitle: Kalman Filter and Neural Network Algorithms Based Observer Estimation Benchmark
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study examines three different methods for predicting vehicle speed: Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). EKF models the movement state of the vehicle by linearizing non-linear systems. This method is particularly effective in reducing prediction errors and increasing model accuracy. MLP, trained with supervised learning, is a neural network architecture that produces an output from various inputs. An MLP model, trained with data collected from the vehicle, has been evaluated comparatively with other methods in this study. LSTM is successful in processing time series data and can model long-term dependencies and transient effects when working with time-dependent data like vehicle dynamics. This study analytically compares the linearization capability of EKF and the ability of MLP and LSTM to model complex patterns and temporal dependencies.

articleTitle: Computation of Robust Stability Delay Margin for Time-Delay DC Motor Speed Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive robust stability analysis for a DC motor speed control system that incorporates communication delays and parametric uncertainties. An efficient approach based on Kharitonov's Theorem is used to determine delay margins that guarantee the stability of the system. Kharitonov's Theorem is a method for analyzing the stability of polynomials with uncertain coefficients. In this study, Kharitonov's Theorem and the elimination of exponential terms method are used together to compute robust stability delay margins that ensure the robust stability of the speed control system with parametric uncertainties. The accuracy of stability delay margins and the robustness of the system are verified by time-domain simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization After Hardware Security in Analog Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In recent years, hardware security has become a significant concern in both the design and the production phases for electronic devices worldwide. Violations of a designer's intellectual property pose substantial financial challenges. While various research studies on hardware security have focused on defence strategies, attack methods, and generally securing a design, the effects on the design process are often overlooked. However, many locking mechanisms significantly impact circuit performance, especially in analog circuits. This impact makes the design process longer and more laborious. In this work, we resize transistors in a circuit after locking using automation to obtain the performance before security or better. With this approach, we propose a combination of optimization methods with security implementations to achieve an optimum security integration process.

articleTitle: An Analysis on Quantum Radar Systems for Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Quantum radar is an alternative to classical radar for target detection. Quantum radar systems utilize a quantum physics term known as quantum entanglement for target detection, which has higher correlation that cannot be achieved by classical sources. The results of the quantum radar analysis have shown that employing a pair of entangled sources has an advantage about a 6 dB in target detection compared to the classical counterpart. These analyses have also been tested experimentally in both optical and microwave frequency domains. These experimental setups have shown that this supremacy level might be achieved under ideal conditions, but it is not possible with the current experimental setups. Nevertheless, employment of quantum physics laws is a new field of study for engineering discipline, with the development of measurement instruments researchers might reach this superiority level.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with Segmented Stator for Robotic Actuators
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Robotic systems require high performance robot joints to achieve advanced mobility capabilities. Recently, innovations in permanent magnet technology, material science, gearbox topologies, and control techniques have facilitated the emergence of unique design and manufacturing approaches, specifically for the electric motors used in the drive mechanism of these structures, known as servo actuators. This study focuses on the design of an inner rotor, surface mounted permanent magnet, frameless synchronous motor with specifications of 48 VDC, 100 W, and 3000 rpm, intended for use in robot joints with gripper. Optimization studies, integrating the segmented stator design, are conducted to enhance the operational performance, environmental interaction, and production efficiency ofthe joints. The advantages and disadvantages of integrated and segmented stator structures are compared. Cogging torque is analyzed, and techniques to reduce this effect is explored. Preliminary sizing is performed using analytical methods, and optimization studies are completed using the finite element method.

articleTitle: Driver Behavior Assessment Based on Vehicle Data and Passenger Feedback Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Evaluating driver behavior in fleet operations is essential for increasing driving safety, improving fuel economy, and optimizing overall driving performance. This study presents the development of a machine learning-based subjective evaluation model designed to assess driver behavior during acceleration and deceleration maneuvers, considering different speed ranges, pedal inputs, and perceived levels of aggressiveness. A structured experimental design was applied, involving the creation of specific driving maneuvers and the formulation of targeted questions to capture subjective feedback on driver behavior. The model utilizes real-time data collected throughout driving maneuvers and a questionnaire designed to measure passengers' perceived levels of safety and comfort. The developed model aims to establish a reliable correlation between measurable driving parameters and perceived driving quality, allowing subjective experiences to be evaluated within an objective framework. This approach has the potential to contribute to personalized driving experiences. Future studies aim to adapt this model to different driving conditions and vehicle types, thereby expanding its applicability.

articleTitle: 600W/28V Phase Shifted Full Bridge DC-DC Converter Design
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The application of soft switching techniques for increasing the power density and efficiency in DC-DC converters is prominent. Phase Shifted Full Bridge (PSFB) DC-DC converters are widely used in high frequency and high power applications due to their Zero Voltage Transition (ZVT) feature. In this study, a 600 W peak current mode controlled PSFB converter operating in the 250-400 V input voltage range is designed. A synchronous rectifier and a passive suppression cell are used in the converter. The elements used in the converter have been determined and a simulation study has been carried out in the PSIM programme. It is shown that zero-voltage switching occurs at full and half load conditions. At 350 V nominal input voltage, 100 kHz switching frequency and full load conditions, the efficiency was found to be 95.5% as a result of the simulation study.

articleTitle: Akciğer Hastalıklarının Teşhisi için Hiyerarşik Sınıflamaya Dayalı Bir Yöntem
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a model was developed to diagnose healthy individuals and those with COVID-19 or other viral pneumonia respiratory diseases using hierarchical classification. COVID-19 X-ray images were used, and the VGG19 convolutional neural network (CNN) was employed for classification tasks on these images. The main objective is to achieve high accuracy in distinguishing between healthy and sick cases, followed by detailed classification of disease types. The hierarchical model consists of a primary classifier to separate healthy and sick samples, followed by a sub-classifier that differentiates between COVID-19 and other viral pneumonia cases. Minimal preprocessing steps were applied to achieve high accuracy through this multi-layered classification system, yielding 100% accuracy in distinguishing healthy and sick cases, 97.5% accuracy in sub-classification of diseases, and an overall accuracy of 98.94% for the hierarchical model. These results highlight the potential of hierarchical classification in disease diagnosis using medical imaging.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of OFDM Based Underwater Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this paper, an underwater communication model utilizing Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM) has been developed, and its outcomes and evaluations have been presented. Scientific formulas related to underwater medium losses and modulation parameters have been employed, with the data being divided into sub-symbols to account for underwater losses. The received symbols have then been reassembled to allow for the analysis of performance parameters. The model has been parameterized, and the effects of changes in parameters such as Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), Bit Error Rate (BER), and underwater medium losses have been analyzed. The results indicate that frequency and distance have a more significant impact on communication performance in non-periodic data transfer compared to other parameters.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Frequency Selective Surface Geometries Designed for the X-Band Using Simulation and Modeling Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the electromagnetic performances of four different Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) designs in the X-band (8.212.4 GHz) frequency range have been comparatively analyzed. The Gridded Double Square Loop, Double Circular Patch, Cross Dipole, and Double Square Loop designs were simulated using CST Studio Suite, ANSYS HFSS, and Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM), and the permeability, reflectivity, and resonance characteristics of each structure were examined in detail. The simulations revealed that the designs are optimized for X-band applications, and each design demonstrates high performance in both wideband and narrowband applications. A high degree of similarity was obtained between the ANSYS HFSS and CST simulation results, and the accuracy of the results was also supported theoretically by comparing them with the ECM method. The findings of this study indicate that the FSS designs presented here can be effectively used in X-band radome applications.

articleTitle: Investigations of Capacitance Change In Antenna Design for Smart Stent Development
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: After stents, which are widely used in the treatment of artery blockages, are implanted, the condition of the artery is generally monitored only through additional angiography. In this study, capacitance changes in antenna design were investigated with the aim of developing a smart stent to monitor the artery's condition externally. Considering frequency ranges where electromagnetic waves have deeper penetration into human tissue, various antennas were designed for this application, and the effects of capacitance changes in the 30 MHz to 500 MHz range on the antenna's return loss and inter-antenna coupling were observed. The results of this study demonstrate that frequency shifts caused by the increase in capacitance of a MEMS-based capacitor on thesmart stent, due to increased pressure in a narrowing artery, can be detected. Simulation results showed that as capacitance increases, there is a progressive shift in the antennas' resonance frequencies.

articleTitle: Cost-Effetive Power Grid Scheme for Fishing Vessel with Clean Grid Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In the contemporary maritime industry, operations focused on reducing carbon emissions on ships are becoming increasingly prevalent due to the mandatory regulations established by leading-organizations aiming to lower these emissions. In this context, alternative solutions such as the use of alternative energy sources, energy-efficient operations, and electric/hybrid propulsion systems are being employed. This study proposes a cost-effective electrical grid scheme with a clean grid converter for a fishing vessel. The proposed system utilizes a shaft generator/motor, which exhibits high energy-saving performance in the shipbuilding sector, and features a grid structure that differs through the use of a clean grid converter to create a clean AC busbar, based on the connection method. The system is designed to have both a variable frequency/voltage AC bus and a fixed frequency/voltage clean AC bus. The configuration and equipment are presented through a single-line-diagram, and the relevant advantages and disadvantages of system are evaluated.

articleTitle: Design and Thermal Analysis of a High Power Density Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Passenger Cars
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The rapid increase in the use of electric vehicles today has further highlighted the importance of electric motors, one of the most critical power transmission components of these vehicles. Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) have become one of the most preferred motor types in electric vehicle applications due to their high torque and power density. This study provides a detailed examination of the electromagnetic design process and thermal analysis of PMSMs intended for use in passenger vehicles. The design process involves the calculation of key electromagnetic parameters, the development of an initial motor model, and its analysis using the finite element method (FEM). The analysis, conducted with ANSYS Electronics software, evaluates critical performance metrics such as magneticfield distribution, torque generation, and power density. Additionally, the motor's thermal behavior under operational conditions is analyzed using ANSYS MotorCAD software.

articleTitle: Design of RF Transceiver Module
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In today's electronic communication and defense industry, the need for high-frequency and reliable systems is steadily increasing. These systems play a critical role by ensuring uninterrupted and secure data transmission during military operations. In this article, a Transciever (transmit-receive) module operating in the S-band frequencies has been designed. The S-band, commonly used in defense and communication applications, offers long-distance communication with low noise. The transmission module includes a power amplifier and an RF converter, while the receiving module incorporates an SPDT switch, interdigital band-pass filter, and low-noise amplifier. The system, developed to be compatible with time-division multiplexing (TDM) architecture using a single antenna, was designed with frequencies used in data link systems in mind.

articleTitle: Doppler Frequency Estimation and Tracking of Iridium NEXT Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, with their wide coverage area and high signal strength, constitute an important source of signals of opportunity (SoOP). In this study, Doppler frequency estimation and tracking based on the orbit prediction of Iridium NEXT, one of the LEO satellites, are addressed. Two models are used to predict the Doppler frequency. Estimation algorithms, QSE and HAQSE, based on DFT interpolation, are applied to these models, and their performances are evaluated in detail through simulations for three different sampling frequencies. Simulation results demonstrate that both models can estimate the Doppler frequency with high accuracy even at low SNR values, and that the proposed methods are both reliable and effective for LEO satellite systems.

articleTitle: A CNN-Based Deep Learning Method for Total Harmonic Distortion Estimation in Power Quality Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In recent years, the existing studies on deep learning methods applied in the field of power quality ggenerally deal with the classifying power quality problems. In the proposed study, the main harmonic analysis of a signal is aimed at performing the total harmonic distortion (THD) amount of the signal with a CNN deep learning based method. The neurons in the structure of CNN, which is specially designed for image processing, are structured in 3 dimensions, just like an image, as width, height and depth. In the preliminary simulation results of the study, THB analysis was performed to show the accuracy of the proposed method. The training of the deep neural network was done using the first 5,000 images out of 10,000 artificially created images and the THB values of these images. The training success was tested with the remaining 5 thousand images of the dataset. The test and estimated THB values were compared. When the estimated THB values were compared with the test values, it was seen that quite successful results were obtained.

articleTitle: Performance of Microstrip Antennas in Textile Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this work, a textile microstrip patch antenna design has been developed for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) applications. The dimensions of the microstrip antenna were determined using theoretical calculations, and 5.8 GHz was chosen as the operational frequency. three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation tools were used to evaluate the microstrip antenna that was constructed based on these dimensions. Examining the behavior of a textile microstrip patch antenna at various bending angles on a cylindrical surface, conformal conditions were used to evaluate the antenna's performance for application on the body (e.g., the arm or torso).To perform conformal simulations of the textile microstrip patch antenna, a human arm model was additionally integrated into the design. Additionally examining fundamental antenna parameters such as return loss and radiation pattern, a SAR (Specific Absorption Rate) analysis was performed to demonstrate that the antenna is suitable for body-worn applications. The textile microstrip patch antenna was produced,and measurements of reflection coefficient and radiation pattern were conducted.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Crowded Scene
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The use of cameras has increased, particularly in public areas like hospitals and city centers, mainly to detect and record anomaly events. Therefore, the automatic analysis of camera footage is important. This study proposes an algorithm that can detect anomalies in camera footage using optical flow map images and an autoencoder deep learning model, evaluating its performance with UCSD datasets. Separate training for each frame and determining a unique anomaly threshold for each test video enhanced performance. The performance of the proposed method was measured using the accuracy metric The proposed method achieved 81% accuracy on UCSD Ped-1 and 82% on UCSD Ped-2.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The increase in energy demand creates new needs for the development of energy storage systems and battery technology. Since lithium-ion batteries, which are frequently used in electric vehicles due to their characteristic features, may pose risks such as fire, toxic gas release and electric shock if used outside their operating limits, the use of battery management systems that will ensure that lithium-ion cells are used under appropriate operating conditions is an important issue. Battery management systems are important in increasing reliability and strengthening battery estimates. This paper aims to provide perspective for future research by explaining the parameters and methods used in estimating the remaining useful life of lithium-ion batteries between 2021 and 2023 and studies that are not sufficiently covered in the literature.

articleTitle: Compact Slow-Wave Transmission Line Design with High Effective Dielectric Constant
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of transmission lines with high propagation constants using slow-wave architecture integrated with coplanar waveguides (CPWs) in 65nm BULK CMOS technology. The slow-wave structure enables the design of more compact and efficient transmission lines by reducing the signal's propagation speed. Electromagnetic simulations were conducted using HFSS software within the 0 to 250 GHz frequency range, with a detailed analysis of performance metrics such as propagation constant, attenuation, effective dielectric constant feff), and quality factor. The results indicate that slow-wave transmission line (SWTL) achieves the same transmission as designed CPW structure while occupying 30% less area, significantly minimizing losses in compact form. Furthermore, the SWTL provides high quality factor up to high frequencies of 250 GHz, offering distinct advantage in millimeter-wave and particularly sub-terahertz applications with more efficient transmission compared to conventional structures. This design stands out as low-loss, space-efficient solution for high-frequency RF systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of 270VDC Electrical Power Distribution System Architectures in more Electric Aircraft Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In the aviation industry, as a result of rapid development in electrical technology, mechanical, pneumatic and hydraulic systems ae being replaced with their highly efficient electrical equivalent. Moreover, mission and avionic systems equipment, which have challenging electrical characteristics, are developed. In order to meet the increasing electrical power demand of the aircraft systems, development of high voltage More Electric Aircraft electrical power systems topologies and power electronic devices that make these architectures possible, are required. In scope of this study, More Electric Aircraft concept is detailed reviewed with related electrical sub-systems. B787, F-35 and F- 22 modern civil and military aircraft models that have 270VDC power distribution system architecture and system components are analyzed.

articleTitle: Determination of Positive and Zero Sequence Impedance Measurements and Parameters in AC Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The calculations and measurements aimed at determining the parameters of transmission lines—key components of power systems—have been a significant subject of research for many years. This study provides a detailed explanation of the positive and zero sequence impedance measurement methods used to identify the parameters of AC transmission lines, along with standardized test setups and mathematical techniques for obtaining line parameters. Subsequently, all the mentioned impedance measurement tests and procedures were conducted on a transmission line model in a laboratory environment. Upon analyzing the results, it was found that the estimated line parameters, such as series resistance, reactance, inter-phase capacitance values, ground capacitances, and ground resistance, were accurately determined when compared to the actual line parameter values.

articleTitle: Stabilization of a Fixed-Wing Aircraft with a Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion-Based PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The effectiveness and stability of flight control systems for aircraft under challenging operational conditions are of critical importance. This paper presents a nonlinear dynamic inversion (NDI)-based controller design for a six degrees of freedom nonlinear fixed-wing aircraft model. The model considered is a Boeing 747-200, a wide-body, long-range jet passenger aircraft. The NDI controller is utilized for controlling the aircraft's attitude and dynamic behavior. To enhance the stability and performance of the aircraft system, a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller is integrated into the NDI controller structure. To simulate real flight conditions, the system actuators are considered to operate under noise, and an additional PI- structured filter is designed for the NDI structure to minimize the adverse effects of this noise. Simulation results show that the proposed NDI and PI-structured control system maintains system stability and performance despite external noise disturbances.

articleTitle: Investigation of New-Generation Aircraft Electrical Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study examines the electric power distribution systems and architectures used in the developing concepts of Electric Aircraft (EA), More Electric Aircraft (MEA), and Hybrid Electric Aircraft (HEA) within the aviation industry. First, the concepts of MEA, HEA, and EA are discussed, along with their development since their inception. The advantages and disadvantages of the arrangement of the electric power distribution system within the aircraft are presented. Subsequently, different topologies used in electric power distribution systems are compared based on reliability, weight, cost, and maintainability. These topology architectures are analyzed in terms of the use of AC and DC voltages at different levels and the effects of system frequency. In addition, the use of electrical power distribution topologies in the new generation of aircrafts in service is discussed. Lastly, popular architectures of electric propulsion systems are examined. Based on the outcomes obtained from the study, the current and future state of aircraft electric power systems are discussed.

articleTitle: Modified SWIN-IR Based Super Resolution Approach for Thermal Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: While RGB cameras are inadequate in low light conditions, thermal cameras offer a solution. However, since the resolution of thermal images is low, super-resolution methods are used to improve these images. Due to the large size and high cost of highresolution thermal camera sensors, super-resolution methods are highly preferred especially in compact security camera solutions. In this study, a modified Swin image restoration (SwinIR) approach using a modified Swin transform is proposed for super resolution in thermal images. In the study, the modified SwinIR algorithm is compared with other solutions. The results show that the proposed modified SwinIR approach outperforms the other methods. The success of the model is evaluated by PSNR (Peak SignaltoNoise Ratio) and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) metrics. The PSNR value of the proposed approach was calculated as 33.56 and the SSIM value was calculated as 0.9145, thus providing the best result.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Electromagnetic and Thermal Performance of an Axially-Slitted Eddy Current Brake
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study aims to develop a new disk structure for eddy current brakes and improve the thermal performance of the conductive disk. In a braking system with a 5A excitation current, 1500 RPM nominal speed, 8 poles, dual-sided, and aluminium disks, the effect of axial slot geometries on braking torque was analysed using the finite element method (FEM). Thermal analyses of the disk structure with the most optimal electromagnetic slot geometry were also conducted. As a result of the analyses, an axial-slotted disk structure, not previously found in the literature, was developed. A temperature difference of approximately 10°C was observed between the one-piece and six-piece axially slotted designs. Although the designed disk has a lower braking torque compared to the original disk, it offers significant thermal advantages.

articleTitle: Overview of Hexagonal QAM Based Constellation Schemes and Applications for Index Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of hexagonal QAM (HQAM) techniques that improve energy efficiency and spectral efficiency, and analyzes their impact on the currently widely used index modulation techniques. In particular, the integration of HQAM with advanced index modulation techniques such as spatial modulation (SM), quadrature spatial modulation (QSM) and media-based modulation (MBM) is discussed. It is shown that HQAM significantly reduces energy consumption during transmission by providing a more homogeneous symbol distribution compared to conventional square QAM structures. Analysis on Rayleigh fading channels reveals that HQAM, when combined with index modulation techniques, significantly improves energy savings and provides an optimal solution for systems with high data rates. Furthermore, BER performance comparisons show that the proposed HQAM-based schemes offer similar performance to conventional QAM modulation with index modulation techniques, but with superior energy efficiency. This indicates that HQAM is poised to play an important role in future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Development of Object Detection Models Compatible with Edge TPU Accelerator for Low-Cost Single-Board Computers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the rapid advancements in deep learning models over the last decade, artificial intelligence applications such as object detection, object tracking, and audio processing and analysis have become increasingly prevalent in everyday life. These software-based advancements have brought with them the need for high-cost hardware. In this study, low-cost embedded single-board computers, such as Raspberry Pi 4-5 and Jetson Nano, which are frequently used in academia and practice, have been compared in terms of performance while running object detection models, and new solutions have been developed. At the core of these solutions lies the Edge TPU co-processor, designed for lower-performance single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi, where the computational load is handled by the CPU. The object detection models developed for single-board computers have been trained to be compatible with the Edge TPU, and real-time object detection was performed using a camera, with performance metrics being calculated.

articleTitle: Mass Estimation of Heavy-Duty Vehicle Using Machine Learning with Simulation-Generated Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a large amount of synthetic data was generated using data obtained from heavy-duty vehicles and a validated vehicle simulation model, which produced different driving cycles and trailer masses. A machine learning model and deep neural network models were then used to estimate the total mass of the vehicle with the generated synthetic data. In addition to signals such as vehicle speed, acceleration, torque, and gear shifts, the study recorded various signals from the power unit and driver inputs to produce more detailed outputs for statistical purposes. After performing a consistency analysis of the data, various machine learning algorithms were compared to determine the most suitable model, and the results of the model with the lowest error were evaluated and compared with previous study. This approach aims to reduce costs and minimize error risks by estimating the vehicle's mass without the use of sensors, thereby reducing the potential for sensor manipulation.

articleTitle: Eperimental Determination of the Performance Characteristics of a Medium Power Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: On a global scale, interest in permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) is continuously increasing, as their applications expand, particularly with the growth of renewable energy use and the electrification of transportation. It is also evident that PMSMs are also being increasingly used in high-performance robotics applications, which require not only accuracy and high performance but also speed controllers that provide flexibility and efficiency in both design process and application. Over the past decade, alongside rapidly advancing technological developments and the development of the power electronics integrated into these motor structures, energy efficiency and enviromental sustainability have maintained their importance in modern technology. This study reports the results of dynamic tests conducted in a laboratory environment using the Field-Oriented Control (FOC) method to examine the performance characteristics of a medium-power (110kW) Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor.

articleTitle: Model for Positioning Stationary Battery Energy Storage Systems for Energy Efficiency in Urban Rail Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Urban rail transport systems consume significant amounts of energy, which makes energy efficiency improvements essential for sustainable urban mobility. This paper analyzes the role of stationary energy storage systems (SESS) in improving the energy efficiency of urban rail transport systems. Various SESS technologies, such as lithium-ion batteries, are examined for their ability to store energy from regenerative braking and redistribute it during peak demand. Key factors such as headway, line gradient, regenerative energy amounts and receptivity of urban rail transport system are considered. The results provide a model proposal for optimizing the placement of stationary energy storage systems for energy flow management in urban rail transport systems. Simulation-based analysis and case studies show that integrating SESS can significantly optimize energy utilization in urban rail systems.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Battery Sizing Strategies for Energy Storage Integrated Charging Stations for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles have initiated a significant transformation in the automotive sector, thanks to the advantages they offer over internal combustion engine vehicles in terms of environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. Supported by increasing market demand and government incentives, these vehicles are becoming widespread globally and are beginning to replace internal combustion engine vehicles. However, the widespread adoption of electric vehicles is not only limited to advancements in vehicle technology but also requires the development of key components such as battery storage systems, charging infrastructure, and grid integration. In this study, efforts to extend battery life and increase energy density have been examined in detail. Studies on the integration of different energy storage systems at charging stations, load balancing strategies, and optimization of charging demand have been thoroughly analyzed. Finally, various optimization algorithms and methods used to improve the grid integration of electric vehicles and energy quality parameters have been discussed comparatively. Methods developed to minimize grid imbalances, voltage fluctuations, and power quality issues have been examined, and the effectiveness of the algorithms has been analyzed.

articleTitle: Frequency Tracking of Unknown Sinusoidal Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This article gives a way for estimating the frequency of an unknown sinusoidal signal. This approach is used within the evaluation board which suggests its effectiveness in appropriately estimating the signal frequency. The article discusses the theoretical basis of the NTA-LS(Newton Rhapson and Least Square) method and describes the method used in detail. Experimental outcomes are supplied to show the effectiveness of the approach. The article concludes that the NTA-LS method is a reliable and proper technique for estimating sinusoidal signal frequencies, and its software in the development board presents a practical solution so for real-time signal processing applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Parameter Estimation Methods for Determining the Parametersof the Battery Electrical Equivalent Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery chemistry has become the preferred choice in modern electrical energy storage systems. While it offers many advantages, its reactive nature can lead to hazardous situations. To prevent this, parameters such as voltage, current, temperature, and state of charge (SOC) must be monitored. In order to carry out this monitoring process, the battery's behavior needs to be mathematically modeled. For this purpose, parameters were determined for equivalent circuit models of varying degrees using different curve-fitting methods. These parameters were derived from test data of A123 Systems' ANR26650M1-B and Samsung's INR 18650 20R battery types. Models created through different curve-fitting methods were then compared with the test data. As a result of this study, a curvefitting method was identified that provides a fast, easy, and highly consistent equivalent circuit model.

articleTitle: Some Methods to Increase the Gain of the Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Developed for the Breast Cancer Hyperthermia Applicator
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a series of processes were conducted to improve the directivity and gain of the Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA), designed for use in the breast cancer hyperthermia applicator. Biomedical hyperthermia is the process of creating a temperature difference of approximately +7 °C in tumor tissue by transmitting electromagnetic waves through antennas positioned in various configurations around the breast. The antenna design phase is crucial because the radiating antenna must achieve maximum temperature increase in tumor tissue with optimal focus while sparing healthy tissues. Steps taken to develop a compact, low-cost, high-gain, and high-directivity Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna are presented.

articleTitle: Battery Capacity Determination of Electric Vehicle Under Variable Temperature Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative test method for evaluating the effects of sudden temperature changes on battery capacity. Unlike existing test methods, this method aims to measure the discharge capacity of the battery during abrupt temperature variations using a single test approach. In the test conducted in this study, a fully charged battery was subjected to partial discharge after sudden temperature changes, and then the temperature was returned to the reference value, allowing the discharge to continue until the minimum voltage was reached. In this way, the effect of temperature fluctuations on the usable capacity was observed. Using the same test method, the battery was discharged to the minimum voltage at low temperatures. After the temperature was returned to the reference value, the discharge process continued, and as a result, it was observed that sudden changes in temperature had no effect on capacity. These findings provide a new methodological contribution that can be applied in the battery industry and battery modeling techniques.

articleTitle: Development of a P2 Hybrid Electric Vehicle Model and Optimization of the Regenerative Braking System in MATLAB Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Regenerative braking is a critical component in the advancement of hybrid and electric vehicles, enhancing energy efficiency and reducing brake wear. This project aims to optimize regenerative brake systems through a comprehensive analysis utilizing MATLAB Simulink. The study focuses on the benefits of regenerative braking in hybrid and electric vehicles, aiming to minimize energy loss during braking and maximize the recovery of kinetic energy. By simulating a hybrid car with a regenerative brake system in MATLAB Simulink, the project evaluates the performance and efficiency gains achieved through regenerative braking, emphasizing its significance in reducing brake wear and enhancing energy regeneration performance. The project underscores the importance of regenerative braking as a key innovation in sustainable transportation, highlighting its potential to contribute to energy conservation and environmental sustainability in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Optimizing Carbon Emissions in EV Charging Stations: A Combined Approach of Two-Stage Optimization and Multi-Energy Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The integration of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations into current energy grids has issues relating to energy management and carbon emissions, but is essential to the global shift toward sustainable transportation. This study suggests a combined strategy to develop a low-carbon and cost-effective EV charging infrastructure: a Two-Stage Optimization Framework paired with Multi-Energy Integration methods. The Two-Stage Optimization Framework promotes the utilization of renewable energy and dynamically changes energy consumption in real time to minimize emissions, employing complex optimization algorithms to balance grid energy needs and carbon trading. Complementing this approach, Multi-Energy Integration— including Power-to-Gas (P2G) and Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) —captures residual emissions and stores excess renewable energy for future use. This integrated approach maximizes energy efficiency while preserving grid stability by minimizing carbon emissions at both the energy generation and consumption phases. According to simulation results, combining these techniques can significantly lower carbon emissions and operating costs, which makes it a feasible strategy for optimizing EV charging stations in order to meet the carbon neutrality target.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection and Assessment of Barcodes on Document Images
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this work, the detection and evaluation of barcodes used in the digitization and tracking processes of internal correspondence of Yurtiçi Kargo Servisi AŞ. were performed. To ensure that all correspondence conducted on paper within the company is digitized, stored, and tracked, barcode labels are affixed to the documents. Barcode numbers are used for searching, responding, and reporting documents in the digital environment. Previously, documents and the barcodes on them were scanned with a special scanner hardware, and the documents were recorded in the system along with the barcode number. However, this situation introduced dependency on specific model hardware and increased costs. In this study, barcodes on documents were detected using scanned document images. For this purpose, a UNet deep neural network model was trained. Barcode images detected by the model were rotated to make them readable by barcode reader libraries. The barcode value was recorded in the system along with the digital version of the document. The system developed as a result of our study has yielded successful results and has been implemented in the internal correspondence of Yurtiçi Kargo Servisi AŞ.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Selective Surface-Based Patch Antenna Array for Ultra-Wideband Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a frequency-selective surface (FSS)-based patch antenna array design was developed to create a high-gain antenna structure for ultra-wideband (UWB) radar systems operating within the 3.1 – 4.8 GHz range. Initially, two-element and four-element patch antenna arrays were constructed. Subsequently, FSS reflectors were employed to suppress the back lobes and enhance the gain. To ensure the FSS exhibited effective reflective characteristics within the specified frequency band, the S11 and S21 parameters of the unit cell structure were optimized. The unit cells were periodically arranged and positioned behind the antenna arrays at a specific air gap distance. The designed FSS structure resulted in a gain increase of 3.55 dBi for the two-element array and 3.41 dBi for the four-element array. Additionally, S11 measurements of the designed antenna arrays were conducted, revealing alignment with the simulation results. These findings indicate that FSS-based patch antenna arrays offer high-performance antenna solutions for UWB radar applications.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Photovoltaic Panel, Battery and Supercapacitor System
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In the present study, a hybrid system modeling consisting of a photovoltaic (PV) panel, battery, supercapacitor, DC-DC converter, and 1 kW load is discussed. Incremental conductance (INC) algorithm is used for maximum power point tracking (MPPT) and the fast response capability of this algorithm enables PV panels to produce maximum power under variable conditions. The simulation study of the hybrid system is carried out in a MATLAB/SIMULINK environment and the power profile of the PV panel, battery, and load is examined. Voltage, current, and charge characteristic curves of the battery and supercapacitor are examined. Simulation results show that a hybrid storage system responds quickly to sudden load changes and thus increases system performance significantly. This study has revealed that hybrid PV panel-battery-supercapacitor systems offer a potential solution to improve energy storage efficiency.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Reference Baseline Consumption Model for Energy Efficiency Measurement and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In Energy Efficiency Efficiency Projects, the IPMVP (International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol) methodologies are employed to measure and verify energy savings based on pre- and post-intervention analyses of energy consumption However, these methods, which depend on low-resolution data and basic regression models, often fall short in accurately calculating target reference consumption and efficiency. Advances in measurement technology now enable real-time energy efficiency analyses with high-resolution data. Additionally, integrating these datasets with sophisticated machine learning models has been observed to improve the accuracy of reference consumption calculations. This study aims to improve the consistency of reference consumption calculations by developing machine learning-based reference consumption models. The piecewise regression, SARIMA, and XGBoost models developed in this research were tested across four distinct facilities equipped with high-resolution data, and their performance was systematically evaluated.

articleTitle: Elektrikli Araç Bataryalarının İkincil Hayat Kullanımı Kapsamında Sabit Enerji Depolama Sistemlerine Entegrasyonu
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In order to reduce waste and utilize resources efficiently, secondary use scenarios are becoming increasingly important before recycling used electric vehicle batteries. The reuse of vehicle batteries in energy storage systems is preferred over direct recycling, both reducing environmental impacts and providing economic benefits. This approach makes it possible to reduce the carbon footprint and increase sustainability by utilizing the full capacity of batteries. In this paper, technical details are presented on the use of the batteries from the electric vehicle in a solar electric vehicle charging station as a stationary energy storage system by testing at the module level and integrating the appropriate battery management system. The system has been developed for the first time in Turkey in accordance with the mass product target for direct consumer use.

articleTitle: LoRa Supported Location Detection for Man Overboard (MOV) Situations
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study presents an alternative positioning method for "man overboard" scenarios, a critical safety issue in maritime environments, where traditional GNSS systems may fail or become inoperative. Considering the risk of GNSS systems losing functionality in situations such as warfare, disasters, or crises, an algorithm has been developed for use in local areas. The algorithm operates using the trilateration method (Circle Intersection Method) based on RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) parameters and is capable of accurately detecting the position of a person who has fallen overboard up to a distance of 2 km. The results demonstrate that the algorithm provides an effective solution in such scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an LLc Resonant Converter with a NOminal 24V 1000W Output for Battery Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The LLC resonant topology, which is highly efficient and has low electromagnetic interference, is a popular structure in DC-DC converters. LLC resonant converters can operate at high frequencies, and their structure is suitable for soft switching. Due to their high-frequency operation, circuit designs can be created in smaller sizes, which allows for increased power density. Consequently, the use of LLC resonant converter topology is also increasing in battery chargers. In this study, an LLC resonant converter structure was designed for a battery charger. The topology of the converter, which has a 24V DC output and 1000W rated power, is shown. The necessary parameters were defined using design equations. Simulations were conducted under different conditions with this topology and these parameters. Through the simulations, the design parameters obtained from the equations were verified, and waveforms were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Review of Parallel Connected MOSFETs and Current Sharing in Power Electronics Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the increasing integration of power electronics into all aspects of life, the demand for high-power converters has also risen significantly. In applications where high power is required, the parallel connection of semiconductor switches plays a critical role in enhancing the system's current-carrying capacity and, consequently, its power transmission capabilities. In this study, the use of parallel-connected MOSFETs in power electronic circuits, the factors affecting current sharing and the methods used to improve current sharing are discussed. Initially, parameters that disrupt current sharing in parallel-connected MOSFETs are examined comparatively, and their effects on current distribution are analyzed. After the parameters that cause unbalanced distribution of current between MOSFETs are determined, the active and passive methods proposed in the literature to improve current sharing are reviewed and their impacts on current distribution are discussed comparatively.

articleTitle: A Detailed Examination of Material Choices for Windings in Dry-Type Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Dry-type transformers are commonly used in a range of applications, from power distribution to industrial sectors. One of the most important factors in transformer design is the selection of conductor material, with copper and aluminum being the main options. This study aims to compare copper and aluminum windings in dry-type transformers for the first time according to the Turkish TEDAŞ MLZ specifications, focusing on their performance, efficiency, and weight. The study also examines how electrical losses and physical characteristics affect the efficiency, size, weight, and reliability of transformers. Interestingly, in dry-type transformers, using copper windings doesn't provide any clear technical advantage over aluminum unless there are specific power needs. Moreover, copper's coefficient of thermal expansion is less compatible with resin than that of aluminum. By providing these insights, the research will assist transformer designers and power providers in making informed material choices.

articleTitle: The Effects of the Multi-Slice Skewing Applied to the Rotor on the Performance of a Flux Switching Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Flux-switching generators are one of the types of generators commonly used in wind turbine applications, particularly in microgrids. The torque ripple and harmonic content of flux-switching generators are significantly high due to the salient pole structure of the stator and rotor teeth. In this study, a multi-layer skewing method was applied to the rotor of a 260 W flux-switching generator, and its effects on the generator's average torque, torque ripple, and efficiency parameters were analyzed. The obtained results indicated that, due to the dominance of the second harmonic, the skewing angle did not have a significant effect on the output parameters. Furthermore, the influence of the number of layers on the generator's output parameters and production difficulty was examined.

articleTitle: Battery Charging System Design with Modified Boost Type Rectifier fed LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, a battery charge system with a 3 kW output power was designed using a half bridge LLC resonant converter for the Lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery preferred in electric vehicle applications. The system aims to reduce switching losses and increase system efficiency by using one of the soft switching techniques, Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS). In the single phase grid-fed system, Modified Boost type Rectifier (MBR), one of the bridgeless boost type rectifier was used as the power factor correction (PFC) circuit. It was observed that the MBR circuit prevented circulation current in Semi Bridgeless Boost type Rectifier (SBBR) circuit and it provided ease of control due to the use of fewer switches. The average current control method was used in the MBR circuit. The total harmonic distortion (THD) value was calculated as 1.33% in the system operated with PFC circuit. The designed system was tested on a battery with 55V/15Ah capacity in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Effect of the Mechanical Alignment of the Winding on Leakage Reactance
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Power transformers are a critical and costly component of power systems, making their longevity essential for maintaining system reliability. The design of these transformers plays a significant role in determining their inductance and reactance, which directly impacts their mechanical strength. This study explores how axial displacements of the windings affect the leakage reactance of transformers. We analyzed four scenarios: moving the entire low voltage winding and the entire high voltage winding to both the upper and lower sides along the axial direction. Our results show that both positive and negative displacements lead to a similar increase in leakage reactance. This finding highlights a key relationship between winding positioning and electromagnetic performance, emphasizing the importance of precise mechanical alignment in transformer design and operation. Ultimately, these insights can help optimize transformer performance under various displacement conditions, enhancing reliability and efficiency in power systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of High-Power Density Phase-Shifted Full Bridge DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, the design and performance of a 2.5 kW full-bridge phase-shifted PWM DC-DC converter are examined. The converter operates at a switching frequency of 100 kHz, providing an output voltage of 250Vand an output current of 10A. Digital control is implemented through a microcontroller, allowing precise adjustment of the output voltage and current. High efficiency and low losses are achieved through soft-switching (SS) techniques. The circuit features both constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) control modes, making it suitable for various applications. The high switching frequency offers size and cost advantages, while also enhancing the reliability and performance of the circuit. This design provides an efficient and flexible solution for high-power power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Asenkron Motorların Alçak Gerilim Şebekeleri Üzerindeki Dinamik Davranışlarının Analizi ve Etkileri
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Induction motors are critically important due to their widespread use in industry and energy efficiency advantages. However, the dynamic effects of these motors on low-voltage grids pose significant challenges, particularly in terms of voltage drops and grid stability. The aim of this study is to analyze the effects of induction motors on grid voltage drops and explore how these effects can be mitigated. In this study, the impact of parameters such as voltage drops, grid short-circuit power, transformer capacity, transformer impedance, and cable length during motor start-up is evaluated using ETAP software. The findings indicate that the high starting currents and low power factors of the motors may lead to voltage drops in the grid; however, these drops can be minimized by increasing transformer capacity and optimizing impedance values.
