Consequently, it is recommended to develop motor control strategies, along with appropriate transformer and cable selections, to mitigate the negative effects of motors on the grid

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Quaternion Based Orientation Estimators with Experimental Data from Inertial Measurement Units
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, different quaternion based filters for orientation estimation using inertial measurement units (IMU) were examined. Orientation determination methods using quaternion representation were detailed, and the complementary filter, Error State Kalman Filter (ESKF), Madgwick filter, Kalman based XKF3i filter, and Versatile Quaternion-based Filter (VQF) were addressed. Experimental studies were conducted using an optical motion capture system and an MTi-300 IMU, comparing the performances of different filters with the optical system taken as the reference. The results showed that all filters operated with high accuracy under a root mean square error (RMSE) below 0.2°. The VQF algorithm provided the best tracking performance of the experimental data, and its modular approach was observed to be effective in reducing error.

articleTitle: The Quantum Revolution in Telecommunications: 6G and Solutions for MobileOperators
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In general, quantum technologies and quantum algorithms possess transformative potential for next-generation communication systems. Particularly with the unprecedented data speeds, ultra-low latency, and seamless global connectivity promised by 6G, these technologies are expected to offer significant opportunities for telecommunications and mobile network operators. The integration of quantum computing can play a role in optimizing network operations, improving resource management, reducing energy consumption, and increasing data processing efficiency. For mobile network operators, this will result in significant progress in key performance indicators (KPIs) such as scalability, reliability, and security. Furthermore, quantum cryptography will be of critical importance by introducing new security standards for real-time data protection. This paper will focus on a mobile network operator�s perspective and explore potential solutions. It will assess the synergy between quantum technologies and telecommunications, focusing on key topics such as network latency, bandwidth optimization, and energy efficiency. By leveraging quantum computing, the paper will explore how future telecommunications networks can become faster, more secure, and more sustainable.

articleTitle: Robust Delay-Dependent Stability Analysis of Pitch Angle Control Systems in Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The aim of this study is to conduct a robust stability analysis, using the Kharitonov's Theoreö, of the controller gains that guarantee system stability for the blade pitch angle control system of wind turbines in the presence of uncertainties in the system parameters. The Kharitonov method is a technique used to analyze the stability of polynomials with uncertain coefficients. For the pitch angle control system to be robustly stable, the four polynomials derived from the characteristic equation must be stable. In this study, the maximum time delay values, defined as the Stability Delay Margin (SDM), at which the closed-loop system will be marginally stable, will be analytically computed using the methods of exponential term elimination and Kharitonov's approach together. Finally, the verification of robust stability delay margins and the robustness of the system have been demonstrated through simulation studies conducted in the time domain.

articleTitle: 1200V Series-Connected GAN-IGBT Hybrid Switch with Single Gate Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: GaN FETs offer higher switching speeds and lower gate drive losses compared to IGBTs. Their low parasitic capacitance allows for achieving higher switching frequencies. Due to the limited Vds voltage of GaN FETs, they must be connected in series for high-voltage power conversion applications, necessitating voltage balancing. This study proposes a gate driving scheme and circuitry to control an 800V / 16A hybrid switch using a single gate driver while balancing voltage across the series-connected GaN FETs. As a result of using the hybrid configuration, conduction loss on GaN FETs has been reduced by 70.7%, and the cost of the switching unit has decreased significantly, making it an alternative low-switching loss and high power switching unit.

articleTitle: Solving XOR in Spike Neural Network (SNN) with Component-off-the-Shelf
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper addresses the solution of the XOR problem with Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) in order to improve energy efficiency and computational performance as Moore's Law approaches its limits. SNN is capable of solving nonlinear problems while saving energy by mimicking the working principles of biological neurons. For this purpose, a SNN consisting of 12 neurons was implemented on a breadboard using the Leaky Integrate and Fire (LIF) model. In the input layer of the network, 50 Hz and 100 Hz signals are processed with frequency sensitive filters. With the help of bandpass and low-pass filters, additive and inverting operational amplifiers, the XOR problem is successfully solved.

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Polarized Antenna Design for GSM and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band and dual-polarized antenna design operating at 1.8 GHz and 3.6 GHz frequency bands. The 1.8 GHz frequency is typically used for mobile communication systems (e.g., GSM), while the 3.6 GHz frequency is suitable for 5G wireless communication applications. The antenna provides both vertical and horizontal polarization across two distinct frequency bands, making it highly applicable to wireless communication systems requiring multi-band and dual-polarized antennas. The antenna is fed using an aperture-coupled feeding method, ensuring high isolation and minimal interference. According to the simulation results, the antenna achieves low return loss and high gain. This study contributes to the potential applications and future development of dual-polarized antennas in modern wireless communication systems [1]

articleTitle: A Modified Sampling Rate for a Continuous Sampling using Dirac Comb
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this paper, a modified sampling rate, which is smaller than the usual Nyquist rate while allowing reconstruction of the signal, is determined for bandlimited signals using Amplitude Modulation (AM). The proposed modified rate is based on the fact that the discrete Fourier spectrum of the sampled signal contains the AM modulated versions of the original spectrum at integer multiples of the sampling frequency. Using that result a continuous time function is defined and it is used to remove the distorted parts of the signal spetrum due to aliasing. The proposed method is novel and valid for impulse sampling in continuous time. However, the method cannot remove the aliasing in discrete time due to the cyclic nature of the discrete time transforms. The study is going on to devise a valid method in discrete time.

articleTitle: Application of a 100 Mm Linear Potentiometer for Speed Measurement in a Linear Motion System Using Stm32F410 Microcontroller: Hardware Design and Software Development
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In today's industrial automation, robotics, and performance evaluation of mechanical systems, precise speed measurements are essential. For these systems to operate efficiently and accurately, it is crucial to accurately determine the speeds of linear-moving components. The linear potentiometer, which is a fundamental component of this system, precisely measures a 100 mm distance by determining the length of the piston rod. This ensures that the system's speed measurements are performed with high precision and reliability. The developed system is optimized in terms of both hardware and software, with hardware-based filters helping to reduce noise and interference, while software-based filters further validate the signal. This combination enhances the accuracy and reliability of speed measurements. The developed speed measurement system is portable and can be easily mounted thanks to the suction cups on it. With these features, the system has a wide range of applications in industrial settings and research projects. This paper examines the design and software details of the developed system and shares the results obtained through calibration and validation processes.

articleTitle: A Review of Bidirectional LLC Converter Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In this study, bidirectional LLC resonant converters used in electric vehicles, energy storage systems and charging stations, which have taken a wide place in the literature in recent years, have been examined and a comparison of these converters has been made. Information about the converters' schematics, operating principles, voltage gain curves and important features has been given. In this context, important features of bidirectional LLC resonant converters such as power density, efficiency, resonant frequencies, maximum gains, control methods and soft switching have been discussed. As a result, a detailed comparison has been made in terms of the converters, circuit structure, input and output voltage, output power, operating frequency range and resonant frequency, magnetizing inductance, number of active and resonant elements used and efficiency.

articleTitle: Feasibility Assessment of Wireless Charging Application on Istanbul Metrobus Line
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Dense urbanization in megacities and the climate crisis demand innovative public transport solutions. Bus systems account for over 80% of global public transport traffic, highlighting their importance for operational efficiency. This paper assesses the feasibility of wireless charging for the Metrobus line in Istanbul, a key public transport operation. Using AVL CruiseM, a Metrobus vehicle model was created to simulate daily movements based on track and vehicle speed data. Findings indicate that wireless charging at intermediate and main stops can meet daily movement targets while reducing battery capacity costs. Future advancements in charging technology and fleet management are expected to further enhance operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Modeling the Effect of Vehicle Mass and Center of Gravity Height on Adaptive Cruise Control and Lane Keeping Assist Systems Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: It is not feasible to conduct road tests for all scenarios related to Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) functions due to time, cost, and safety constraints. In this study, the effects of changes in vehicle weight and center of gravity (CoG) height on vehicle behavior in Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) and Lane Keeping Assist System (LKAS) scenarios were examined. Relevant standards and regulations for ACC and LKAS were reviewed, and test matrices for simulations were created. The environmental and vehicle conditions for the selected scenarios were simulated, and tests were conducted. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) specific to each maneuver were calculated using simulation data. Machine Learning (ML) models were developed to understand whether there is a relationship between the calculated KPIs and changes in vehicle variants. The relationships between vehicle variants and KPIs were reported as a result of the study.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Data Augmentation Method on 2D Segmentation of 3D Point Cloud Data
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: 3D deep learning methods are widely used in point cloud semantic segmentation. Semantic segmentation of 2D images obtained from 3D point clouds is also an alternative method. This method allows usage ofseveral techniques for data augmentation and preprocessing which might not be available in 3D and could be advantageous in segmentation of classes without height characteristic such as road classes. However, clarity and data loss might appear in the process of dimensionlality reduction. This could negatively effect the segmentation performance. To address this issue, a Super-Resolution data augmentation approach has been proposed. A simple deep learning model was trained using high resolution satellite images of urban areas. Model outputs were used as a data augmentation technique to train binary segmentation models. Results show that SR data augmentation improves segmentation performance of the road class and it could be a viable option for segmentation of images created from 3D point clouds.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Frequency Hopping System: Applications and Improvements Over Turkey
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a deep learning-based frequency hopping system aimed at minimizing interference and optimizing spectrum usage in wireless communication systems. Applied across different regions of Turkey, this GPS-supported system utilizes deep learning algorithms to analyze regional radio frequency traffic and select the most appropriate frequency. The system dynamically performs frequency selection based on both geographic location and time, minimizing interference and significantly improving communication quality. This innovative approach is designed to provide reliable, seamless, and secure communication, particularly in military and civilian applications. The study focuses on applications in Turkey, improvements in frequency management, and spectrum efficiency. This system offers a crucial solution for enhancing communication in areas with high radio traffic in the future

articleTitle: IEC61850 Based Substation Automation and Centralized Protection & Control Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Developments in microprocessors based digital relaying have led to the digitalization of power substations. In the following years, continuous advances in digitalization and use of IEC61850 based communications technologies in the digital protection systems have led to the developments of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IED) and their widespread use. IEC61850 protocol has enabled IEDs produced by different vendors to work together. This interoperability provides interaction among to protection systems and control systems, and the necessary data communications during the performance of these systems. After all these developments, the idea of full automation of power networks, instead of digital substation, has emerged. This paper includes the advances in IEC61850 based substation automation, centralized protection and control based substation automation, and also discusses possible future developments in the related area.

articleTitle: Analysis of Stability Regions Load Frequency Control with Time Delay Systems Considering Rotor Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: This paper presents the stability regions of the time-delayed load frequency control (LFC) system enhanced by dynamic participation of wind turbine (WT). Although the integration of WT into LFC enhances the dynamic stability of the system, the complexities of the system increase. Therefore, it is crucial to determine the stability regions and boundaries of the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller in the parameter space for the LFC system including WT dynamics. In this study, the stability regions of the system in the controller parameter space are determined using the stability boundary locus method. The obtained stability regions are verified by time-domain simulations in MATLAB/Simulink. The obtained findings show that the integration of WT including inertia control and deloading control loops into LFC system improves the stability regions.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Axial-Flux Induction Generator Topologies in Variable Speed Wind Turbine Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Wind energy has inevitably become widespread due to the increasing world population, sustainability problems, and the green energy standards that are increasingly coming to the forefront. Axial-flux induction generators (AFIG) are one of the significant generator topologies that can meet the expectations from wind energy systems. It is possible to derive various AFIG topologies by using different stator and rotor combinations. Each topology gains significance according to the requirements of the application. In this paper, 8 kW, 400V/50 Hz single stator-single rotor (SSSR) and double stator-single rotor (DSSR) topologies have been examined, and both analytical and finite element analysis results have been compared through the equivalent circuit design approach for these topologies. It has been demonstrated, both by finite element analyses and the outputs of the developed algorithm, that the DSSR-AFIG architecture outperforms the SSSR-AFIG in terms of both power density and efficiency.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Determining the Optimal Battery Size for Suitable Speed Profiles in Rail Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Rail systems, as a cornerstone of modern transportation networks, provide sustainable transportation solutions in urban and rural areas. With the increasing population and urbanization, the necessity to enhance the efficiency, safety, and cost-effectiveness of rail systems has become paramount. This study examines the research on the optimization of technical components such as speed profiles, algorithm types, and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) sizing to improve the performance of rail systems. Optimal speed profiles enhance system efficiency by reducing energy consumption and travel times. Advanced algorithms play a critical role in boosting operational efficiency. Furthermore, accurate ESS sizing increases energy efficiency and reduces costs. This literature review aims to comprehensively analyze recent studies on these three key components of rail systems, providing valuable insights that will guide future research and projects.

articleTitle: Effects of Wind Turbine Height Variation on Hybrid Power System Feasibility
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: In carbon neutrality plans, hybrid power systems (HPS) are critical to the growing popularity of prosumers. For regions with higher wind potential, a sensitive study of wind energy in optimization frameworks with different objective functions will enhance competition against the dominant solar market. In this study, HPSs located at various case areas with higher wind potential are optimally sized for community electricity consumption and minimum cost objectives. The feasibility results of the optimum sizes are evaluated for the effects of increasing wind turbine (WT) hub heights considering flexible and constrained electricity sales. The results show that higher WT heights in Gemlik and �anakkale will optimize performance. It has also been proven that higher WT heights will increase carbon emissions up to 930.1 tons/yr, while restricting electricity sales by 40% will increase the excess electricity by up to 21.4% and reduce the renewable fraction by up to 7.5%.

articleTitle: Literature Review on Multiband, High Gain Antenna Design for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: After the revolution that 5G technology has made in the field of communication, the amount of data has increased. At te same time, the need for higher speed is increasing day by day. High-speed wireless communication devices are needed to enable easier transmission of increased data at high speed. The need for high-speed transmission of data requires more complex miniaturized antennas that can operate in wide bands. Operation in the terahertz (THz) bands, or terahertz frequencies, focuses on the design of high gain antennas with much wider band, multi-band operation to meet the need for high speed communication. In this paper, we review the multiband antenna designs in the literature that operate in the THz frequency band and gain enhancement methods at THz frequency. Metamaterial structured antennas, the use of graphene as a radiating element and array antenna designs are examined and conclusions are presented. Challenges and dilemmas that arise in this direction are also discussed. This work is planned to be a basis for further studies.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis of Air Quality in Rail Transit Systems: A Case Study of the Istanbul Metro
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: Rail transit systems are preferred worldwide for their convenience, safety, and speed. However, their enclosed environments feature high particulate matter (PM) concentrations and diverse particulate content. PM concentration varies due to factors such as outdoor air quality, tunnel design, the chemical composition of rail components (wheels, tracks, braking systems, power sources), power systems, braking mechanisms, train speed and frequency, passenger numbers, ventilation and air conditioning systems, cleaning frequency, and other operational conditions. The Istanbul rail transit system transports over 2 million passengers daily, accounting for approximately 20% of the city's transportation load. This study aims to assess current air quality in the Istanbul rail transit system and observe the effects of platform screen doors and ventilation systems. Measurements were conducted at 7 underground stations, including PM<sub>1</sub> (particles smaller than 1 micron), PM<sub>2,5</sub> (particles smaller than 2.5 microns), and PM<sub>10</sub> (particles smaller than 10 microns), as well as thermal comfort parameters (temperature, humidity, air flow rate) and gas measurements (CO and CO<sub>2</sub>). The results indicate that controlling the content of rail transit dust can significantly improve air quality.

articleTitle: An Overview of Utilizing Regenerative Braking Energy from Rail Transit Vehicles for Charging Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: The adoption of electric vehicles has been rapidly increasing in recent years due to technological advancements, environmental concerns, and geopolitical factors in the energy sector. However, one of the most significant challenges to the widespread deployment of electric vehicles is the difficulty in managing the impact of their charging requirements and fluctuating electricity demand on power systems, as well as meeting the growing energy demand. The expansion of rail-based public transportation has also become inevitable, particularly in densely populated metropolitan areas. Integrating electric vehicle charging stations into existing transportation infrastructure enables rail transit systems to accommodate the demand for charging power. Moreover, the integration of renewable energy sources in parking areas facilitates the development of various energy management strategies. Recent studies have focused on developing strategies for the optimal management of electric vehicle charging demand and the uncertainties associated with renewable energy production. This paper examines examples of the implementation of storage systems and electric vehicle charging stations integrated into rail transportation infrastructure and explores how these models have been addressed in different studies.

articleTitle: A Swift Survey about Semantic Analysis in Document Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 15th National Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ELECO)
abstract: With the advancement of technology, the number of textual data kept in electronic form is increasing day by day. It is now of great importance of produce summary from textual data and verify its consistency with original resources. If the summary is abstractive, then it needs somehow approve summary information. Semantic analysis plays important role in the automatic document verification process, and it is the purpose of this study. Firstly, important studies that apply different types of semantic measurement techniques are discussed in general. Then, the basic components of semantic analysis are listed. Moreover, the relationships between these components are specified. Subsequently, the metrics used in semantic analysis measurement are comprehensively given. Finally, open problems related to semantic analysis in the document verification process are dealed with discussions.
